| **"A man shall say: 'Mother Zion!' and a man was born in her, and He, the Most High, hath established her."** (*Μήτηρ Σιών, ἐρεῖ ἄνθρωπος· καὶ ἄνθρωπος ἐγεννήθη ἐν αὐτῇ...*, Ps. 86:5 LXX) | **"Save us, O Son of God, Who wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor, who sing to Thee: Alleluia."** |

"Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen." **"O Only-begotten Son and Word of God"** (*Ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς καὶ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ*).

#### Antiphon 3

| Verses of the Antiphon | Refrain |
| :--- | :--- |
| **"I will sing of Thy mercies, O Lord, forever."** (*Τὰ ἐλέη σου, Κύριε, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ᾄσομαι*, Ps. 88:2 LXX) | Dismissal Troparion of the Feast: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain, O Christ our God..."** (*Μετεμορφώθης ἐν τῷ ὄρει Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός...*) |
| **"The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord, and Thy truth in the church of the saints."** (*Ἐξομολογήσονται οἱ οὐρανοὶ τὰ θαυμάσιά σου, Κύριε*, Ps. 88:6 LXX) | Dismissal Troparion of the Feast: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain..."** |
| **"Blessed is the people that knoweth the joyful shout."** (*Μακάριος ὁ λαὸς ὁ γινώσκων ἀλαλαγμόν*, Ps. 88:16 LXX) | Dismissal Troparion of the Feast: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain..."** |
| **"O Lord, in the light of Thy countenance shall they walk, and in Thy name shall they rejoice all the day."** (*Κύριε, ἐν τῷ φωτὶ τοῦ προσώπου σου πορεύσονται, καὶ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ἀγαλλιάσονται ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν*, Ps. 88:16–17 LXX) | Dismissal Troparion of the Feast: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain..."** |

Entrance Hymn (Isodikon): **"For with Thee is the fountain of life; in Thy light shall we see light"** (*Ὅτι παρὰ σοὶ πηγὴ ζωῆς, Κύριε, ἐν τῷ φωτί σου ὀψόμεθα φῶς*, Ps. 35:10 LXX)... **"Save us, O Son of God, Who wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor, who sing to Thee: Alleluia!"** (*Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβὼρ μεταμορφωθείς...*). The Dismissal Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast, the Trisagion, the Epistle and the Gospel. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"Now things unheard of have been heard"** [3] (*Τὸ Νῦν τὰ ἀνήκουστα ἠκούσθη*, see the Seventh Ode). Communion Hymn: **"In the light of the glory of Thy countenance, O Lord, we will walk forever"** (*Ἐν τῷ φωτὶ τῆς δόξης τοῦ προσώπου σου*, Ps. 4:7; 88:16 LXX); [the Dismissal Troparion:] **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain"**, and Dismissal.

On the evening of the Feast, whatever day it may be, instead of the Prokeimenon of the day, we chant the Great Prokeimenon: **"Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath pleased, He hath done"** (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ*, Ps. 113:11 LXX), with its verses.

### Saturday after the Feast

4.    On Friday evening, Vespers is chanted according to the order of the Menaion, and at the conclusion the Paraklesis. Dismissal Troparion: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain"** (*Μετεμορφώθης ἐν τῷ ὄρει*); the Priest: **"Have mercy on us, O God"** (*Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*), etc., and Dismissal.

# Month of August: Saturday after the Feast (Concl. §§ 5–6); Sunday after the Feast (Heading, §§ 7–8, § 9 Opening)

## Σαββάτῳ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν (Τέλος §§ 5–6)· Κυριακῇ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν (Ἐπιγραφή, §§ 7–8, § 9 Ἀρχὴ)

5.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικὸν καὶ τὴν τακτικὴν ᾿Ακολουθίαν τοῦ Ὄρθρου, εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους τὰ εἰς τὴν Θ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς Ἑσπέρια Τῆς παναγίας ἐνδόξου Μεταμορφώσεως εἰς δ΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὁ φωτί σου ἅπασαν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἁγιάσας, Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει· μετὰ τὴν Ἐκτενῆ, τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα Ἐν ὄρει τῷ Θαβώρ, (ζήτει τῇ Θ΄ τοῦ μηνός) καὶ τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον.

6.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ ᾿Αντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβὼρ μεταμορφωθείς. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν . . . ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβώρ. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

### Κυριακῇ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν.

7.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ς΄ καὶ μεθέορτα δ΄, Δόξα, Δεῦτε ἀναβῶμεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος Κυρίου (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτήν), Καὶ νῦν, τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν τῆς ἑορτῆς, Νῦν ἀπολύεις, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

8.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ· εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ τὰ μεθέορτα ἀντὶ τῶν Θεοτοκίων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες, ὁ Ἀναστάσιμος, καὶ ὁ εἷς τῆς ἑορτῆς· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα μεθέορτον ἅπαξ, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Σταυρὸν χαράξας καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον καὶ μεθέορτον ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄ καὶ μεθέορτα δ΄, Δόξα τὸ Ἑωθινόν, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

9.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῆς ἑορτῆς. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον Ἐπὶ τοῦ ὄρους μετεμορφώθης,

# Month of August: Saturday after the Feast (Concl. §§ 5–6); Sunday after the Feast (Heading, §§ 7–8, § 9 Opening)

## Saturday after the Feast (Concl. §§ 5–6); Sunday after the Feast (Heading, §§ 7–8, § 9 Opening)

5.    On Saturday, after the Midnight Office and the regular order of Matins, at the Praises: the Vespers Stichira of August 9: **"Of the all-holy and glorious Transfiguration"** (*Τῆς παναγίας ἐνδόξου Μεταμορφώσεως*) to 4; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Sanctifying the whole world with Thy light"** (*Ὁ φωτί σου ἅπασαν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἁγιάσας*); **"To Thee belongeth glory"** (*Σοὶ δόξα πρέπει*); after the Insistent Litany, the Aposticha: **"On Mount Tabor"** (*Ἐν ὄρει τῷ Θαβώρ*, see August 9), and the Dismissal Troparion.

6.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast: **"Save us, O Son of God, Who wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor..."** (*Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβὼρ μεταμορφωθείς*). After the Little Entrance: **"O come, let us worship... Who wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν... ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβὼρ μεταμορφωθείς*). At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen and taken unto Thyself, O Lord"** (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω καὶ προσελάβου, Κύριε*, Ps. 64:5 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

### Sunday after the Feast

7.    On Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 6 Stichira of the Resurrection and 4 of the Afterfeast; "Glory...": **"Come, let us ascend into the mountain of the Lord"** (*Δεῦτε ἀναβῶμεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος Κυρίου*, see the Litiya); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Feast; **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*); the Trisagion Prayers; the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Feast once, and Dismissal.

8.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection twice, and that of the Feast once; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, and the Sessional Hymns of the Afterfeast in place of the Theotokia; the Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection, and one of the Feast; after the Third Ode, the Afterfeast Sessional Hymn once; after the Sixth Ode, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Menologion. Katavasiai: **"Inscribing the Cross"** (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*), and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then we chant the Magnifications: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, and of the Afterfeast once. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Afterfeast; "Glory...": the Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

9.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 hymns from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Feast. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Feast, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain"** (*Ἐπὶ τοῦ ὄρους μετεμορφώθης*)...[^383]

# Month of August: Sunday after the Feast (Concl. § 9); The Apodosis of the Feast (August 13, Heading, §§ 10–12, § 13 Opening)

## Κυριακῇ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν (Τέλος § 9)· Ἡ Ἀπόδοσις τῆς ἑορτῆς (Ἐπιγραφή, §§ 10–12, § 13 Ἀρχὴ)

᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.
      Τῇ αὐτῇ Κυριακῇ ἑσπέρας, ὁ τῆς σειρᾶς Ἑσπερινὸς ψάλλεται κατὰ τὴν διάταξιν τοῦ Μηναίου, γίνεται Εἴσοδος, καὶ μετὰ τὸ Νῦν ἀπολύεις ψάλλεται ἡ Μεγάλη Παράκλησις ὡς εἴθισται.

### Ἡ ᾿Απόδοσις τῆς ἑορτῆς.

10.   Τῇ ΙΓ΄ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μηνός, ἡ ᾿Ακολουθία ψάλλεται ἀπαραλλάκτως ὡς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῆς ἑορτῆς, ἐξαιρουμένων ἐν τῷ Ἑσπερινῷ τῶν ᾿Αναγνωσμάτων, καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ τῆς Λιτῆς, τοῦ Πολυελέου καὶ τοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· ἐν δὲ τῇ Λειτουργίᾳ, ᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τὰ τῆς ἡμέρας.

11.   Εἰ τύχοι ἡ ᾿Απόδοσις ἐν Κυριακῇ τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς Ἰδιόμελα ς΄, Δόξα τῆς ἑορτῆς, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν τῆς ἑορτῆς, Νῦν ἀπολύεις, τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τῆς ἑορτῆς δίς, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

12.   Τῇ Κυριακῇ, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ ᾿Απολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἀντὶ τῶν Θεοτοκίων, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ Ἀναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες, ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος, καὶ οἱ δύο τῆς ἑορτῆς· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς τὸ Κάθισμα τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ Ἀναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Σταυρὸν χαράξας καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, καὶ ψάλλεται καὶ ἡ Θ΄ [Ὠδὴ] τῆς ἑορτῆς, Ἐξαποστειλάρια τὸ Ἀναστάσιμον καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς δίς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄, Δόξα, Παρέλαβεν ὁ Χριστός, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

13.   Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ ᾿Αντίφωνα τῆς ἑορτῆς· εἰς τὸ β΄ Ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβώρ, τὸ Εἰσοδικὸν Ὅτι παρὰ σοὶ πηγὴ . . . μετὰ τοῦ Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς

# Month of August: Sunday after the Feast (Concl. § 9); The Apodosis of the Feast (August 13, Heading, §§ 10–12, § 13 Opening)

## Sunday after the Feast (Concl. § 9); The Apodosis of the Feast (August 13, Heading, §§ 10–12, § 13 Opening)

...Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.
      On that same Sunday evening, the Vespers in series is chanted according to the order of the Menaion; Little Entrance is made, and after **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*), the Great Paraklesis is chanted as is customary.

### The Apodosis of the Feast

10.   On the 13th of this month, the service [of the Apodosis] is chanted without variation exactly as on the day of the Feast, with the following exceptions: in Vespers, the Readings are omitted; in Matins, the Litiya, the Polyeleos, and the Gospel are omitted; and in the Divine Liturgy, the Epistle and Gospel are of the day.

11.   If the Apodosis falls on a Sunday, on Saturday evening, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 4 Stichira of the Resurrection and 6 Idiomela of the Feast; "Glory...": of the Feast; "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Feast; **"Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart"** (*Νῦν ἀπολύεις*); the Trisagion Prayers; the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Feast twice, and Dismissal.

12.   On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, and the Sessional Hymns of the Feast in place of the Theotokia; the Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection, and the two of the Feast; after the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymn of the Feast once; after the Sixth Ode, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Menologion. Katavasiai: **"Inscribing the Cross"** (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*), and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then we chant the Magnifications: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*), and the Ninth Ode of the Feast is chanted; Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, and that of the Feast twice. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": **"Christ took with Him Peter, James, and John"** (*Παρέλαβεν ὁ Χριστός*); "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

13.   In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast; at the second: **"Who wast transfigured upon Mount Tabor"** (*Ὁ ἐν τῷ ὄρει τῷ Θαβὼρ μεταμορφωθείς*). The Entrance Hymn (Isodikon): **"For with Thee is the fountain of life..."** (*Ὅτι παρὰ σοὶ πηγὴ...*) with **"Who art risen from the dead"** (*Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*); after the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: of the...[^384]

# Month of August: Apodosis of the Transfiguration (August 13, Concl.); Forefeast of the Dormition and Prophet Micah (August 14, §§ 1–3)

## Τῇ ΙΓ΄: Ἀπόδοσις τῆς Μεταμορφώσεως (Τέλος)· Τῇ ΙΔ΄: Τὰ Προεόρτια τῆς Κοιμήσεως καὶ τοῦ Προφήτου Μιχαίου (§§ 1–3)

ἑορτῆς καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς.
Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ὁ τόκος σου, ἄφθορος, Κοινωνικὸν τῆς
ἑορτῆς, Μετεμορφώθης ἐν τῷ ὄρει, ᾿Απόλυσις καὶ ᾿Απόδοσις.

### Τῇ ΙΔ΄. Τὰ Προεόρτια τῆς Κοιμήσεως τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου, καὶ τοῦ Προφήτου Μιχαίου.

1.    Ἐὰν τύχωσι τὰ Προεόρτια ἐν ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, ὁ προεόρτιος Ἑσπερινὸς (καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτόν, ἐννοεῖται, ἡ τελευταία Παράκλησις), καὶ τὸ πρωῒ ὁ Ὄρθρος μετὰ τῆς Λειτουργίας ψάλλονται κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Μηναίου διάταξιν.

2.    Ἐὰν τύχωσιν ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ᾿Αναστάσιμα ς΄ καὶ Προεόρτια δ΄, Δόξα, Τὴν πάνσεπτόν σου Κοίμησιν, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ Προεόρτιον ἅπαξ, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.
      Ἡ δὲ ᾿Ακολουθία τοῦ Προφήτου Μιχαίου ἐν τοῖς ᾿Αποδείπνοις.

3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ, εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ προεόρτιον ᾿Απολυτίκιον καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον δὶς καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον ἅπαξ, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα καὶ ἀντὶ τῶν θεοτοκίων τῆς Ὀκτωήχου τὰ Προεόρτια, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ ᾿Αναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες, ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ Προεόρτιος μετὰ Στίχου Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, τὸ προεόρτιον Κάθισμα ἅπαξ, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ ᾿Αναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι ᾿Ανοίξω τὸ στόμα μου . . . τὸ τέλος ταύτης τὴν Κοίμησιν, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ ᾿Αναστάσιμον καὶ τὸ Προεόρτιον Σοῦ τῆς σεπτῆς Κοιμήσεως ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ Προεόρτια δ΄ Δῆμος τῶν μαθητῶν, Δόξα τὸ Ἑωθινόν, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη,

# Month of August: Apodosis of the Transfiguration (August 13, Concl.); Forefeast of the Dormition and Prophet Micah (August 14, §§ 1–3)

## August 13: Apodosis of the Transfiguration (Concl.); August 14: Forefeast of the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos, and the Prophet Micah (§§ 1–3)

...the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, and the Kontakion. Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"Thy childbearing was shown to be incorrupt"** (*Ὁ τόκος σου, ἄφθορος*); Communion Hymn of the Feast: **"Thou wast transfigured upon the mountain"** (*Μετεμορφώθης ἐν τῷ ὄρει*); Dismissal and Apodosis.

### August 14: Forefeast of the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos, and the Prophet Micah

1.    If the Forefeast of the Dormition falls on any day except Sunday, the Forefeast Vespers (and with it, it is understood, the last Paraklesis), and in the morning Matins with the Divine Liturgy are chanted according to the order of the Menaion.

2.    If the Forefeast falls on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 6 Stichira of the Resurrection and 4 of the Forefeast; "Glory...": **"Thy all-venerable Dormition"** (*Τὴν πάνσεπτόν σου Κοίμησιν*); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"She who is higher than the heavens"** (*Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, that of the Forefeast once, and Dismissal.
      The service of the Prophet Micah is chanted at Compline.

3.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon, and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection twice, and that of the Forefeast once; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, and in place of the Theotokia of the Octoechos, we chant those of the Forefeast; the Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection and of the Forefeast with the Verse: **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us"** (*Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε*); after the Third Ode, the Forefeast Sessional Hymn once; after the Sixth Ode, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Menologion. Katavasiai: **"I shall open my mouth"** (*Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*), with the ending of this: **"her Dormition"** (*τὴν Κοίμησιν*), and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then we chant the Magnifications: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, and that of the Forefeast: **"Celebrating the radiant memorial of thy holy Dormition"** (*Σοῦ τῆς σεπτῆς Κοιμήσεως*) once. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forefeast: **"The community of the disciples"** (*Δῆμος τῶν μαθητῶν*); "Glory...": the Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and...[^385]

# Month of August: Forefeast of the Dormition (August 14, Concl. § 4); The Dormition of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos (August 15, §§ 1–2)

## Τῇ ΙΔ΄: Τὰ Προεόρτια τῆς Κοιμήσεως (Τέλος § 4)· Τῇ ΙΕ΄: Ἡ Κοίμησις τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου (§§ 1–2)

καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

4.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Προεορτίου Κανόνος δ΄. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ Προεόρτιον, τὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Τῇ ἐνδόξῳ μνήμῃ σου. ᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

### Τῇ ΙΕ΄. Ἡ Κοίμησις τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Δεσποίνης ἡμῶν Θεοτόκου.

1.    Ἐν τῷ Μ. Ἑσπερινῷ, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὴν α΄ Στάσιν τοῦ Ψαλτηρίου, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα τὰ Προσόμοια Ὢ τοῦ παραδόξου θαύματος εἰς ς΄, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Θεαρχίῳ νεύματι, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὰ ᾿Αναγνώσματα. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ γ΄ Ἰδιόμελα, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ὅτε ἐξεδήμησας, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον [Ἐν τῇ γεννήσει] ἐκ γ΄ καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

2.    Τὸ πρωῒ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τοῦ Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ἡ Λιτή, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον ἐκ γ΄, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος Ἐξηρεύξατο ἡ καρδία μου, τὰ Καθίσματα ἐκ β΄, οἱ ᾿Αναβαθμοί, τὸ α΄ ᾿Αντίφωνον τοῦ δ΄ ἤχου, τὸ Προκείμενον Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου, τὸ Πᾶσα πνοὴ καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον ᾿Αναστᾶσα Μαριάμ, εἶτα ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμὸς χῦμα, Δόξα, Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου, Καὶ νῦν τὸ αὐτό, ὁ Στίχος Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεὸς καὶ τὸ Ἰδιόμελον Ὅτε ἡ μετάστασις, οἱ Κανόνες ἀμφότεροι μετὰ τοῦ Στίχου Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἡ Ὑπακοή, ἀφ᾿ ς΄ τὸ Κοντάκιον, ὁ Οἶκος καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ, εἶτα ψάλλεται ἡ θ΄ Ὠδὴ μετὰ τῶν Μεγαλυναρίων· εἰς μὲν τὸν α΄ Κανόνα τὸ Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι μακαρίζομέν σε, τὴν μόνην Θεοτόκον, εἰς δὲ τὸν β΄ τὸ Ἄγγελοι τὴν Κοίμησιν τῆς Παρθένου, ὁρῶντες ἐξεπλήττοντο, πῶς ἡ Παρθένος ἀπαίρει ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς εἰς τὰ ἄνω, καὶ ἡ Καταβασία Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι

------------------------------------------------------------------------
[4] Εὐθὺς μετὰ τὴν Καταβασίαν τῆς θ΄ συνηθίζεται ἐνιαχοῦ, ὅπου πανηγυρίζεται ἡ ἑορτὴ αὕτη μεγαλοπρεπῶς, πρὸς πλείονα τάχα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν τῆς Θεοτόκου, ἵνα ψάλλωνται τὰ λεγόμενα ἐγκώμια τῆς Παναγίας, κατὰ μίμησιν τῶν τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν, τῶν ψαλλομένων ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ τοῦ Μ. Σαββάτου. Ἡ Μ. Ἐκκλησία κατακρίνουσα πᾶν ὅ, τι καινοφανὲς καὶ κακόζηλον, ἔστω καὶ γινόμενον πρὸς τιμὴν τῆς Θεοτόκου ἀποδοκιμάζει ταῦτα ἐπισήμως καὶ ἀπαγορεύει μάλιστα αὐστηρῶς.

# Month of August: Forefeast of the Dormition (August 14, Concl. § 4); The Dormition of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos (August 15, §§ 1–2)

## August 14: Forefeast of the Dormition (Concl. § 4); August 15: The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos (§§ 1–2)

...and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

4.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 hymns from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Forefeast. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Forefeast, that of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: **"At thy glorious memorial"** (*Τῇ ἐνδόξῳ μνήμῃ σου*); Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

### August 15: The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos

1.    In Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant the Prosomoia: **"O, the marvelous wonder!"** (*Ὢ τοῦ παραδόξου θαύματος*) to 6; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"By the royal command of God"** (*Θεαρχίῳ νεύματι*). Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings. At the Aposticha: the three Idiomela; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"When thou departedst from this life"** (*Ὅτε ἐξεδήμησας*). The Dismissal Troparion: [**"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ γεννήσει*)] three times, and Dismissal.

2.    In the morning at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Litiya; then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparion three times; then the Psalter reading and the Polyeleos: **"My heart hath poured forth a good word"** (*Ἐξηρεύξατο ἡ καρδία μου*, Ps. 44 LXX). The Sessional Hymns (twice each); the Anavathmoi: the First Antiphon of Tone 4; and the Prokeimenon: **"I will remember thy name"** (*Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου*, Ps. 44:18 LXX). Then **"Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*), and the Gospel: **"Mary having arisen"** (*Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ*, Luke 1:39–49, 56); Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice; "Glory...": **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos"** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); "Both now and ever...": repeat the same. The Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God"** (*Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:1 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"When the translation to heaven"** (*Ὅτε ἡ μετάστασις*). Then the Canons with the Verse: **"Most Holy Theotokos, save us"** (*Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε*). After the Third Ode, the Hypakoe; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion, the Ikos, and the Menologion. The Katavasia: **"Adorned with divine glory"** (*Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ*). Then the Ninth Ode with the Megalynaria: for the First Canon we chant: **"All generations call thee blessed, the only Theotokos"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι μακαρίζομέν σε, τὴν μόνην Θεοτόκον*); for the Second Canon we chant: **"The angels, as they looked upon the Dormition of the Virgin, were struck with wonder at how the Virgin went up from earth to heaven"** (*Ἄγγελοι τὴν Κοίμησιν τῆς Παρθένου, ὁρῶντες ἐξεπλήττοντο, πῶς ἡ Παρθένος ἀπαίρει ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς εἰς τὰ ἄνω*); and the Katavasia: **"All generations . . . The laws of nature are overcome"** [4] (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*). The Exaposteilarion...[^386]

------------------------------------------------------------------------
[4] *Original Printed Footnote:* In some churches, especially where the Feast of the Dormition is celebrated with added magnificence, it has become customary—supposedly for the greater glory and honor of the Theotokos—to chant immediately after the Katavasia of the Ninth Ode the so-called Enkomia [Praises] of the All-Holy One, in emulation of the Enkomia of our Lord, which are chanted at the Matins of Great and Holy Saturday. Censuring any work that strains to appear innovative and that mimics with bad taste a preexisting work—even though this is done in honor of the Theotokos, as in this instance—the Great Church officially disapproves of all such imitations and, in fact, sternly forbids their use.

## Τῇ ΙΕ΄: Ἡ Κοίμησις τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου (Τέλος § 2, § 3 Ἀντίφωνα Α΄–Γ΄ & Εἴσοδος)

      Ἐγενήθη ἐν εἰρήνῃ ὁ τόπος αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ κατοικητήριον αὐτοῦ ἐν Σιών.
      [Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου, Σῶτερ, σῶσον ἡμᾶς.]

#### ᾿Αντίφωνον Β΄.

      ᾿Αγαπᾷ Κύριος τὰς πύλας Σιών, ὑπὲρ πάντα τὰ σκηνώματα Ἰακώβ.
      Δεδοξασμένα ἐλαλήθη περὶ σοῦ, ἡ πόλις τοῦ Θεοῦ.
      Ὁ Θεὸς ἐθεμελίωσεν αὐτὴν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
      {Ἡγίασε τὸ σκήνωμα αὑτοῦ ὁ Ὕψιστος}

#### ᾿Αντίφωνον Γ΄.

      Ἑτοίμη ἡ καρδία μου, ὁ Θεός, ἑτοίμη ἡ καρδία μου.
      Τί ἀνταποδώσω τῷ Κυρίῳ περὶ πάντων, ὧν ἀνταπέδωκέ μοι;
      Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι καὶ τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου ἐπικαλέσομαι.
      [Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει τὴν παρθενίαν...]

      Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει καὶ τὸ Κοντάκιον Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις ἀκοίμητον, ὁ

# Month of August: The Dormition of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos (August 15, Concl. § 2, § 3 Antiphons 1–3 & Entrance)

## August 15: The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos (Concl. § 2, § 3 Antiphons 1–3 & Entrance)

...(thrice). At the Praises: the three Prosomoia in 4; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"At thy deathless Dormition"** (*Τῇ ἀθανάτῳ σου Κοιμήσει*); Great Doxology, and the Dismissal Troparion: **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*).

Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄. Δόξα, Τῇ ἀθανάτῳ σου κοιμήσει, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

# Month of August: The Dormition of the Most Holy Lady Theotokos (August 15, Concl. § 3, Sunday Concurrence §§ 4–6)

## August 15: The Dormition of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos (Concl. § 3, Sunday Concurrence §§ 4–6)

...the Gospel: **"Jesus entered a certain village"** (*Εἰσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς κώμην τινά*, Luke 10:38–42; 11:27–28). At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"All generations . . . The laws of nature are overcome"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*). Communion Hymn: **"I will receive the cup of salvation"** (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*, Ps. 115:4 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

4.    If the Feast occurs on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Great Vespers following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira and the Prosomoia of the Feast to 6; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"By the royal command of God"** (*Θεαρχίῳ νεύματι*). Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings of the Feast. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"When thou departedst from this life"** (*Ὅτε ἐξεδήμησας*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection once, and of the Feast twice, and Dismissal.

5.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon, the Litiya, and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*), and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparia as in Vespers; then the Psalter reading and the Polyeleos: **"My heart hath poured forth a good word"** (*Ἐξηρεύξατο ἡ καρδία μου*, Ps. 44 LXX). At the Sessional Hymns of the First Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and that of the Feast: **"Cry out, O David"** (*Ἀναβόησον Δαβίδ*); at the Second Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and that of the Feast: **"The all-honorable chorus"** (*Ὁ πάντιμος χορός*); then the Third Sessional Hymn of the Feast twice; the Petition, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon of the Feast: **"I will remember thy name"** (*Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου*, Ps. 44:18 LXX). Then **"Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord"** (*Πᾶσα πνοή*), and the Gospel: **"Mary having arisen"** (*Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ*). Then **"Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ"** (*Ἀνάστασιν Χριστοῦ θεασάμενοι*); Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice; "Glory...": **"Through the intercessions of the Theotokos"** (*Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*); "Both now and ever...": repeat the same. The Verse: **"Have mercy on me, O God"** (*Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*, Ps. 50:1 LXX), and the Idiomelon: **"When the translation to heaven"** (*Ὅτε ἡ μετάστασις*). Then the Canons of the Resurrection and the two of the Feast. After the Third Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection, and the Hypakoe: **"All generations call thee blessed"** (*Μακαρίζομέν σε πᾶσαι αἱ γενεαί*) read in a low voice; after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the Menologion. The Katavasia: **"Adorned with divine glory"** (*Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ*); then the Ninth Ode of the Feast with the Megalynaria. The Resurrection Exaposteilarion and that of the Feast twice. At the Praises: 4 hymns of the Resurrection and 4 of the Feast; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"At thy deathless Dormition"** (*Τῇ ἀθανάτῳ σου κοιμήσει*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

6.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast, and at the Second Antiphon: **"Who art risen from the dead"** (*Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). At the Little Entrance: **"Come, let us worship . . . Who art risen from the dead"** (*Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν... ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, of the Feast, and the Kontakion: **"Neither the tomb nor death"** (*Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις*); the Epistle and the Gospel of the Feast. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"All generations . . . The laws of nature are overcome"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*). Communion Hymn: [**"I will receive the cup of salvation"**]...[^388]

᾿Απόλυσις.

### Τῇ ΙϚ΄. Ἡ ἐξ Ἐδέσσης ἀνακομιδὴ τῆς ἀχειροποιήτου Εἰκόνος, ἤτοι τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Διομήδους.

7.    Τῇ ΙΕ΄ τοῦ μηνὸς ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακόν, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ψάλλομεν τὰ γ΄ Στιχηρὰ Προσόμοια τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου, καὶ γ΄ τῆς ἑορτῆς (τὰ τοῦ μικροῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ), Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Δεῦτε τὴν παγκόσμιον κοίμησιν. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον τῆς ἡμέρας. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ τῆς σειρᾶς Δῆμος τῶν μαθητῶν, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν μεθέορτον, ᾿Απολυτίκια Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου, Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

8.    Εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸ Μεσονυκτικόν, ὁ Ν΄ ψαλμός, ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Μηναίου διάταξιν, ὁ Κανὼν τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου, αἱ Καταβασίαι Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ, Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον τῆς σειρᾶς δίς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, τὰ τοῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ γ΄ Προσόμοια τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου Ποίοις οἱ γηγενεῖς ὄμμασιν εἰς δ΄. Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτήν). Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου.

9.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοί, Τροπάρια ἐκ τῆς γ΄ καὶ ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, Τὴν ἄχραντον εἰκόνα σου, Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, καὶ Κοντάκιον Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις, ὁ ᾿Απόστολος (ζήτει Σαββάτῳ πρὸ τῶν Φώτων), καὶ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ, ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι, Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

10.   Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακόν, καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ δ΄, τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου γ΄ καὶ γ΄ τῆς ἑορτῆς (τὰ τοῦ μικροῦ Ἑσπερινοῦ), Δόξα, Δεῦτε φιλεόρτων τὸ σύστημα (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτὴν τῆς ἑορτῆς), Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἄσατε λαοί (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτήν), τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου, Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

7.    On August 15, at Great Vespers following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we sing the three Stichira Prosomoia of the Holy Mandylion, and three of the Feast (from Small Vespers); "Glory... At the Praises: the three Prosomoia of the Holy Mandylion from Vespers: **"With what earthly eyes"** (*Ποίοις οἱ γηγενεῖς ὄμμασιν*) to 4; "Glory... Epistle (see Saturday before Epiphany [1 Tim. 3:13–4:5]), and the Gospel: **"At that time, it came to pass, when the time was come"** (*Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ, ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι*, Luke 9:51–56; 10:22–24). At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord from the heavens"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

10.   If the Feast occurs on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we sing 4 Resurrection Stichira, three of the Holy Mandylion, and three of the Feast (from Small Vespers); "Glory...": **"Come, assembly of feast lovers"** (*Δεῦτε φιλεόρτων τὸ σύστημα*, see the Litiya of the Feast); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Sing, O people!"** (*Ἄσατε λαοί*, see the Litiya). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, **"Thy most pure icon"** (*Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου*), **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*), and Dismissal.

# Month of August: Translation of the Holy Mandylion (August 16, Concl. §§ 11–12); Sunday after the Dormition (Heading, §§ 13–14 Opening)

## Τῇ ΙϚ΄: Ἡ ἀνακομιδὴ τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου (Τέλος §§ 11–12)· Κυριακὴ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν (Ἐπικεφαλίς, §§ 13–14 Ἀρχή)

11.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ ᾿Απολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος. Εἰς τὴν α΄ Στιχολογίαν δύο ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα, καὶ μεθέορτον Καθορῶσαι ἀληθῶς (ζήτει εἰς τὴν ΙΣΤ΄)· εἰς τὴν β΄ Στιχολογίαν αὖθις δύο ᾿Αναστάσιμα, καὶ τὸ ἕτερον μεθέορτον Ἐν χερσὶ τοῦ δι᾿ ἡμᾶς· εἶτα τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ ᾿Αναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος, καὶ ὁ τοῦ ἁγίου Μανδηλίου μετὰ Στίχου Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς Κάθισμα Ἐδέσσης βασιλεὺς καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς Ὁ πάντιμος χορός· ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ ᾿Αναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον τῆς ἡμέρας, αἱ Καταβασίαι Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου, εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἐξαποστειλάριον, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς Τῶν ᾿Αποστόλων ὁ δῆμος ἅπαξ. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ μεθέορτα δ΄ Ὕμνοις σου τὸ σεπτὸν (ζήτει τῷ ΙΣΤ΄), Δόξα τὸ Ἑωθινόν, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

12.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, Τὴν ἄχραντον εἰκόνα σου, Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει, τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις ἀκοίμητον, ᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε. Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

### Κυριακὴ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν.

13.    Τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας, μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρὰ ς΄ καὶ μεθέορτα δ΄, Δόξα, Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα ὑπάρχουσα (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτήν), Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου. Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρόν, καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Ἄσατε λαοί (ζήτει εἰς τὴν Λιτήν), τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

14.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ.

# Month of August: Translation of the Holy Mandylion (August 16, Concl. §§ 11–12); Sunday after the Dormition (Heading, §§ 13–14 Opening)

## August 16: Translation of the Holy Mandylion (Concl. §§ 11–12); Sunday after the Feast (Heading, §§ 13–14 Opening)

...**"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"Thy most pure icon"** (*Τὴν ἄχραντον Εἰκόνα σου*), and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. At the Sessional Hymns of the First Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and that of the Afterfeast: **"Beholding truly"** (*Καθορῶσαι ἀληθῶς*, see August 16); at the Second Stichologia: two of the Resurrection and the other one of the Afterfeast: **"In the hands of Him Who for our sake"** (*Ἐν χερσὶ τοῦ δι᾿ ἡμᾶς*). The Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Then the Canons of the Resurrection and of the Holy Mandylion with the Verse: **"Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"** (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*). After the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymn: **"The King of Edessa"** (*Ἐδέσσης βασιλεύς*) and that of the Feast: **"The all-honorable chorus"** (*Ὁ πάντιμος χορός*); after the Sixth Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Resurrection and the Menologion of the day. Katavasiai: **"Adorned with divine glory"** (*Πεποικιλμένη τῇ θείᾳ δόξῃ*), and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then we chant the Magnifications: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). The Resurrection Exaposteilarion and that of the Feast: **"The community of the Apostles"** (*Τῶν ᾿Αποστόλων ὁ δῆμος*) once. At the Praises: 4 hymns of the Resurrection and 4 of the Afterfeast: **"With hymns to thy venerable body"** (*Ὕμνοις σου τὸ σεπτόν*, see August 16); "Glory...": the Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

12.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and the Beatitudes of the Tone. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, **"Thy most pure icon"** (*Τὴν ἄχραντον εἰκόνα σου*), **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*), of the Patron Saint of the Church, and the Kontakion: **"Neither the tomb nor death"** (*Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις ἀκοίμητον*); Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.

### Sunday after the Feast

13.    On Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Afterfeast; "Glory...": **"She who is higher than the heavens"** (*Ἡ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὑψηλοτέρα ὑπάρχουσα*, see the Litiya of the Feast); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Sing, O people!"** (*Ἄσατε λαοί*, see the Litiya). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, that of the Feast: [**"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*)] once, and Dismissal.

14.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*), and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection twice and that of the Feast once; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. At the Sessional Hymns: two of the Resurrection and one of the Afterfeast in place of...[^390]

### The Apodosis of the Feast

16.    On the 23rd of this month the Apodosis of the Feast takes place, and the service is chanted without variation according to the order set forth in Paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 [of August 15], with the following exceptions: in Vespers, the Psalter reading and the Old Testament Readings are omitted; and in Matins, the Litiya, the Polyeleos, the Gospel, and the Menologion are omitted. In the Divine Liturgy, the Epistle and the Gospel are of the Feast, and the Communion Hymn: **"I will receive the cup of salvation"** (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*, Ps. 115:4 LXX).

17.    If the Apodosis falls on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 4 Resurrection Stichira and 6 of the Feast; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"By the royal command of God"** (*Θεαρχίῳ νεύματι*). Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"When thou departedst from this life"** (*Ὅτε ἐξεδήμησας*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection once, and of the Feast twice, and Dismissal.

18.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon, the Litiya, and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion: **"In giving birth"** (*Ἐν τῇ Γεννήσει*), and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. At the Sessional Hymns: two of the Resurrection and one of the Feast in place of each of the Theotokia. The Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Then the Canons of the Resurrection and the two of the Feast. After the Third...[^391]

At the Praises: 4 hymns of the Resurrection and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": **"At thy deathless Dormition"** (*Τῇ ἀθανάτῳ σου Κοιμήσει*); "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

19.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Antiphons of the Feast; at the Second Antiphon: **"Who art risen from the dead"** (*Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*). After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, of the Feast, and the Kontakion: **"Neither the tomb nor death"** (*Τὴν ἐν πρεσβείαις*). Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday. {Translator’s Note: This rubrical order does not conform with page 36–37 § 42 of the Protheoria, which states: "On the Dormition of the Theotokos and on the Apodosis, the Epistle and the Gospel are always those of the Feast, regardless of the day on which it falls."} At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"All generations . . . The laws of nature are overcome"** (*Αἱ γενεαὶ πᾶσαι . . . Νενίκηνται τῆς φύσεως οἱ ὅροι*). Communion Hymn: **"I will receive the cup of salvation"** (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*, Ps. 115:4 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*); Dismissal and Apodosis.
       After the Apodosis of the Feast, the Katavasiai: **"Inscribing the Cross"** (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς*) are resumed, and the Kontakion: **"Joachim and Anna"** (*Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα*) is said.

### August 29: The Beheading of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John

1.    If the commemoration of the Forerunner falls on any day except Sunday, the service is chanted as set forth in the Menaion.

2.    If it falls on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 4 Stichira of the Resurrection and 6 of the Forerunner; "Glory...": **"While the birthday festival was being held"** (*Γενεθλίων τελουμένων*); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), the Prokeimenon, and the Old Testament Readings. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory...": **"O Forerunner of the Savior"** (*Πρόδρομε τοῦ Σωτῆρος*); "Both now and ever...": **"O Unwedded Virgin"** (*᾿Ανύμφευτε Παρθένε*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, **"The memory of the righteous"** (*Μνήμη δικαίου*), the Theotokion: **"All beyond understanding"** (*Πάντα ὑπὲρ ἔννοιαν*), and Dismissal.

# Month of August: The Beheading of the Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (August 29, Concl. §§ 3–4, Fasting Rubric, § 5 Saturday Concurrence)

## Τῇ ΚΘ΄: Ἡ ᾿Αποτομὴ τῆς τιμίας κεφαλῆς τοῦ Προδρόμου (Τέλος §§ 3–4, Σημ. Νηστείας, § 5 Σάββατον)

Τριαδικὸς κανών, ἡ Λιτὴ τοῦ Προδρόμου καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον τοῦ Προδρόμου, καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὰ ᾿Απολυτίκια ὡς εἰς τὸν Ἑσπερινόν, τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Πολυέλεος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειράν, καὶ ἀνὰ ἓν τοῦ Προδρόμου μετὰ τῶν Θεοτοκίων· ἐν δὲ τῇ γ΄ Στιχολογίᾳ, Κάθισμα τοῦ Προδρόμου καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ ᾿Αναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τοῦ Προδρόμου· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Κοντάκιον καὶ ὁ Οἶκος, εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα τοῦ Προδρόμου Νῦν ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον· ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος Προδρόμου καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Σταυρὸν χαράξας, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, Ἐξαποστειλάρια, τὸ ᾿Αναστάσιμον, τοῦ Προδρόμου καὶ τὸ Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τοῦ Προδρόμου δ΄, Δόξα, Πάλιν Ἡρωδιὰς μαίνεται, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

4.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τοῦ Προδρόμου. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τοῦ Προδρόμου, καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα, ᾿Απόστολος καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Προδρόμου. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως, Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Εἰς μνημόσυνον, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

      Σημ. Τὴν ἡμέραν ταύτην παρελάβομεν νηστεύειν τοὺς εὐσεβεῖς, διὰ τὸν φόνον τοῦ μείζονος πάντων τῶν Προφητῶν Ἰωάννου τοῦ καὶ Προδρόμου τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐὰν τύχῃ ἐν Σαββάτῳ ἢ Κυριακῇ, καταλύομεν ἔλαιον καὶ οἶνον, εὐχαριστοῦντες Χριστῷ τῷ Θεῷ.

5.    Ὅταν τύχῃ ἡ ἑορτὴ τοῦ Προδρόμου ἐν Σαββάτῳ, τὸ ἑσπέρας τῆς αὐτῆς ἡμέρας ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄, τοῦ Προδρόμου τὰ ἐν τῇ σειρᾷ γ΄, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου ᾿Αλεξάνδρου γ΄, Δόξα, Γενεθλίων τελουμένων, Καὶ νῦν τὸ τοῦ ἤχου Θεοτοκίον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, Δόξα [Καὶ νῦν] τοῦ Προδρόμου, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τοῦ Προδρόμου καὶ Θεοτοκίον. Τὸ πρωῒ ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος κανὼν καὶ ὁ τοῦ Προδρόμου· ἐν τῇ γ΄ Ὠδῇ, Κάθισμα τοῦ Προδρόμου, ὡς καὶ τὸ Ἐξαποστειλάριον, τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ τῆς Κυριακῆς.

# Month of August: The Beheading of the Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (August 29, Concl. §§ 3–4, Fasting Rubric, § 5 Saturday Concurrence)

## August 29: The Beheading of the Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (Concl. §§ 3–4, Fasting Rubric, § 5 Saturday Concurrence)

...the Forerunner, and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner, and the Six Psalms.       *Note on Fasting:* On this day we have received the tradition that pious believers fast on account of the murder of John, the greatest of all the Prophets and the Forerunner of our Savior; but if the Feast falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, we partake of oil and wine, giving thanks to Christ our God.

At the Aposticha: "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Forerunner; the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Forerunner, and the Theotokion. In the morning at Matins, the Canons of the Resurrection and of the Forerunner; at the Third Ode, the Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner, as also the Exaposteilarion; the rest of the hymns are those of the Sunday.[^393]

# Month of August: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of the Most Holy Theotokos (August 31, §§ 1–4)

## Τῇ ΛΑ΄: Ἡ Κατάθεσις τῆς τιμίας Ζώνης τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου (§§ 1–4)

### Τῇ ΛΑ΄. Ἡ Κατάθεσις τῆς τιμίας Ζώνης τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου.

1.    Εἰ τύχοι ἡ ἑορτὴ ἐν ἄλλῃ ἡμέρᾳ πλὴν Κυριακῆς, τὴν διάταξιν τῆς ᾿Ακολουθίας ὅρα Ἰουλίου β΄. Ἐν τῷ Ὄρθρῳ Καταβασίαι ψάλλονται Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς καὶ Κοντάκιον τὸ ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς ἐπέχον τόπον Καθίσματος Τὰ καταθέσια τῆς σῆς θείας Ζώνης καὶ καθεξῆς. (Διὰ τὸ σωστὸν Κοντάκιον, ὅρα ὑποσημείωσιν, σελ. 41).

2.    Εἰ τύχοι ἐν Κυριακῇ, τῷ Σαββάτῳ ἑσπέρας μετὰ τὸν Προοιμιακὸν καὶ τὸ Ψαλτήριον, εἰς τὸ Κύριε ἐκέκραξα ᾿Αναστάσιμα ς΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄, Δόξα, Ὡς στέφανον ὑπέρλαμπρον, Καὶ νῦν τὸ α΄ Θεοτοκίον τοῦ ἤχου, Εἴσοδος, Φῶς ἱλαρὸν καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Εἰς τὰ ᾿Απόστιχα, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Στιχηρά, Δόξα, Καὶ νῦν, Φρένα καθάραντες καὶ νοῦν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς Θεοτόκε ἀειπάρθενε ἅπαξ, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

3.    Τῇ Κυριακῇ εἰς τὸν Ὄρθρον, μετὰ τὸν Ν΄ ψαλμόν, ὁ Τριαδικὸς κανὼν καὶ τὰ Τριαδικὰ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, εἶτα τὸ Τρισάγιον, τὸ ᾿Απολυτίκιον τῆς ἑορτῆς καὶ ὁ Ἑξάψαλμος. Εἰς τὸ Θεὸς Κύριος, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον δίς, καὶ τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς ἅπαξ, εἶτα τὸ Ψαλτήριον καὶ ὁ Ἄμωμος, τὰ ἀναστάσιμα Καθίσματα κατὰ σειράν, ἀλλ᾿ ἀντὶ Θεοτοκίου τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς, τὰ Εὐλογητάρια, ἡ Ὑπακοή, οἱ ᾿Αναβαθμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου καὶ τὸ Προκείμενον. Κανόνες ὁ ᾿Αναστάσιμος καὶ ὁ τῆς ἑορτῆς· ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς, Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τῆς ἑορτῆς, εἶτα τὸ Κάθισμα Οἱ τῶν θαυμάτων ποταμοί· ἀφ᾿ ς΄ Κοντάκιον καὶ Οἶκος τὰ ᾿Αναστάσιμα καὶ τὸ Μηνολόγιον, αἱ Καταβασίαι Σταυρὸν χαράξας, καὶ ἅπασα ἡ τάξις τοῦ Ἑωθινοῦ Εὐαγγελίου· εἶτα στιχολογοῦμεν Τὴν τιμιωτέραν, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον Ἐξαποστειλάριον, καὶ τὰ β΄ τῆς ἑορτῆς. Εἰς τοὺς Αἴνους, ᾿Αναστάσιμα δ΄ καὶ τῆς ἑορτῆς δ΄, Δόξα τὸ Ἑωθινόν, Καὶ νῦν, Ὑπερευλογημένη, Δοξολογία Μεγάλη καὶ τὸ Σήμερον σωτηρία.

4.    Εἰς τὴν Λειτουργίαν, τὰ Τυπικὰ καὶ οἱ Μακαρισμοὶ τοῦ ἤχου εἰς δ΄ καὶ δ΄ ἐκ τῆς ς΄ Ὠδῆς τοῦ Κανόνος τῆς ἑορτῆς. Μετὰ τὴν Εἴσοδον, τὸ ἀναστάσιμον ᾿Απολυτίκιον, τὸ τῆς ἑορτῆς, καὶ τοῦ Ἁγίου τοῦ Ναοῦ, Κοντάκιον Τὴν θεοδόχον γαστέρα σου Θεοτόκε* (ζήτει ἀπὸ γ΄ Ὠδῆς), ᾿Απόστολος Εἶχεν ἡ πρώτη σκηνή [ζήτει Νοεμβρίου ΚΑ΄] καὶ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς Κυριακῆς. Εἰς τὸ Ἐξαιρέτως Ἄξιόν ἐστιν, Κοινωνικὸν Αἰνεῖτε, Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς, καὶ ᾿Απόλυσις.

# Month of August: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of the Most Holy Theotokos (August 31, §§ 1–4)

## August 31: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of the Most Holy Theotokos (§§ 1–4)

### August 31: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of the Most Holy Theotokos

1.    If the Feast falls on any day except Sunday, see July 2 for the order of service. In Matins, the Katavasiai: **"Inscribing the Cross"** (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς*) are chanted, and the Kontakion from the Third Ode: **"The deposition of thy divine Cincture"** (*Τὰ καταθέσια τῆς σῆς θείας Ζώνης*) takes the place of the Sessional Hymn, and so on. (For the correct Kontakion, see footnote on page 41.)

2.    If the Feast falls on a Sunday, on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and the Psalter reading, at **"Lord, I have cried"** (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*, Ps. 140 LXX), we chant 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": **"As an all-radiant crown"** (*Ὡς στέφανον ὑπέρλαμπρον*); "Both now and ever...": the first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, **"Gladsome Light"** (*Φῶς ἱλαρόν*), and the Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: the Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": **"Having purified our mind and understanding"** (*Φρένα καθάραντες καὶ νοῦν*). The Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, that of the Feast: **"O Ever-Virgin Theotokos"** (*Θεοτόκε ἀειπάρθενε*) once, and Dismissal.

3.    On Sunday at Matins, after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Trinity Canon and the Trinity Hymns **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, and the Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection twice, and that of the Feast once; then the Psalter reading and the 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. The Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, but in place of the Theotokia, those of the Feast; the Evlogitaria, the Hypakoe, the Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection and of the Feast; after the Third Ode, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, then the Sessional Hymn: **"The rivers of thy wonders"** (*Οἱ τῶν θαυμάτων ποταμοί*); after the Sixth Ode, the Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and the Menologion. Katavasiai: **"Inscribing the Cross"** (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*), and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then we chant the Magnifications: **"More honorable than the Cherubim"** (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*). Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, and the two of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": the Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever...": **"Most blessed art Thou"** (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*); Great Doxology, and **"Today salvation"** (*Σήμερον σωτηρία*).

4.    In the Divine Liturgy, the Typika and the Beatitudes of the Tone to 4, and 4 hymns from the Sixth Ode of the Canon of the Feast. After the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Feast, and that of the Patron Saint of the Church; Kontakion: **"Thy womb which received God, O Theotokos"** (*Τὴν θεοδόχον γαστέρα σου Θεοτόκε*, see the Third Ode); the Epistle: **"The first tabernacle indeed had"** (*Εἶχεν ἡ πρώτη σκηνή*, Heb. 9:1–7, see November 21), and the Gospel of the Sunday. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], **"It is truly right"** (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*); Communion Hymn: **"Praise the Lord"** (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*, Ps. 148:1 LXX); **"We have seen the true light"** (*Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*), and Dismissal.[^394]

# Triodion: Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee (Rubrics of Great Vespers and Matins, §§ 1–2 Opening)

### Notes

[^139]: The Ecclesiastical New Year (Indiction), September 1, St. Simeon the Stylite, and the Synaxis of the Theotokos of Miasena (Violakis, pp. 148–149, September 1, §1). The opening of the Fixed Cycle of the Menaion on September 1 marks the Byzantine Ecclesiastical New Year, designated the Indiction (*Ἀρχὴ τῆς Ἰνδίκτου*, Latin *Indictio*). The term originally designated the fifteen-year imperial Roman and Byzantine fiscal tax assessment cycle established under Emperor Constantine the Great, fixed to September 1 in 312 AD, and later codified as the official civil and ecclesiastical calendar beginning under Emperor Justinian I in 537 AD (Novella 47). In Christian typological theology, September 1 sanctifies the passage of cosmic time, commemorating Christ's inauguration of His public ministry in the synagogue of Nazareth (Luke 4:16–22) when He unrolled the scroll of the Prophet Isaiah and proclaimed "the acceptable year of the Lord" (Isaiah 61:1–2). Concurrently, the Church commemorates the venerable father St. Simeon the Stylite the Elder (c. 390–459 AD), who introduced the ascetic discipline of pillar-dwelling (stylitism) atop a column near Antioch, together with his mother St. Martha; as well as the Synaxis of the Most Holy Mother of God of Miasena (*Μιασηνῶν*), commemorating the miraculous discovery in the ninth century of her wonderworking icon, which had been cast into Lake Miasena in Armenia to preserve it from iconoclastic destruction during the reign of Emperor Leo the Isaurian. On weekdays, Great Vespers features the First Stasis of the First Kathisma of the Psalter (*Blessed is the man*, Psalm 1 LXX), ten Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" (three Prosomia of the Indiction, three of St. Simeon, and four Idiomela of the Indiction), festive Old Testament readings from Leviticus, Isaiah, and Wisdom, and concluding Dismissal Troparia: the Troparion of the Indiction, "O Creator of the universe, Who hast set the times and seasons in Thine own power..." (*Ὁ πάσης δημιουργός*, Tone 2); the Troparion of St. Simeon, "Thou didst become a pillar of endurance, O venerable one..." (*Ὑπομονῆς στῦλος*, Tone 1); and the Theotokion "Hail, full of grace, O Virgin Theotokos..." (*Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*).
[^140]: Weekday Matins & Liturgy of the Indiction, Katavasiai of the Holy Cross, and Sunday Vespers Concurrence (Violakis, pp. 150–151, September 1, §§2–5). At Matins of the Indiction on a weekday, following the Midnight Office and the Hexapsalmos, the Troparia are chanted at "God is the Lord" as at Vespers. The hymnography includes two canons: the Canon of the Indiction (composed by St. John of Damascus, Tone 3) and the Canon of St. Simeon Stylites (Tone 2). A liturgical milestone occurs at the Katavasiai: beginning on September 1, the Church appoints the Katavasiai of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross: "Moses, having etched the cross with his rod, divided the Red Sea for Israel walking on foot..." (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς*, Tone 8). These Katavasiai are chanted continuously through the Apodosis of the Exaltation on September 21. At the Divine Liturgy on weekdays, the Typika and Beatitudes incorporate troparia from Odes 3 and 6 of the Indiction Canon, followed by the Epistle (1 Tim. 2:1–7) and Gospel (Luke 4:16–22) of the Indiction, and the proper Communion Verse (Psalm 64:12 LXX): "Bless the crown of the year with Thy goodness, O Lord" (*Εὐλόγησον τὸν στέφανον τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ τῆς χρηστότητός σου, Κύριε*). When September 1 coincides with the Lord's Day (§§4–5), the Resurrectional service of the Octoechos joins with the Indiction: at Saturday Great Vespers, four Resurrection Stichira, three of the Indiction, and three of the Saint are chanted at "Lord, I have cried", crowned by the Indiction Doxastikon: "O Holy Spirit, Who art bound together with the Father and the Son in eternal timelessness..." (*Ὁ πνεύματι ἁγίῳ*), and the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone.
[^141]: Sunday Concurrence of the Indiction, the Sunday before the Exaltation, and the Miracle of Archangel Michael at Chonae (Violakis, pp. 152–153, September 1 §6 & September 6 §§1–2). When September 1 falls on a Sunday, the Divine Liturgy appoints the Beatitudes divided four of the Resurrection Tone and four of Ode 6 of the Indiction Canon. Following the Little Entrance, the Dismissal Troparia are: the Resurrection Troparion, the Troparion of the Indiction, the Theotokion "Hail, full of grace", the Troparion of St. Simeon, and the Patron Saint of the temple, sealed by the Indiction Kontakion. Violakis records a critical calendar rule regarding the Saturday Indiction: if September 1 falls on a Saturday, the immediately subsequent Sunday is September 2; thus, on the following Sunday (which falls on September 8, or September 7 if an inclusive count was loosely used), the Epistle (Gal. 6:11–18) and Gospel (John 3:13–17) are appointed for the "Sunday before the Exaltation" (*Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῆς Ὑψώσεως*). On September 6, the Church commemorates the Miracle of the Archangel Michael at Colossae in Phrygia (Chonae) (*Τὸ ἐν Χώναις θαῦμα τοῦ Ἀρχιστρατήγου Μιχαήλ*), where the Archangel struck a great rock with his staff to open a subterranean chasm, swallowing two rushing torrents (the Lykokapros and Kouphos) diverted by pagans to submerge the sanctuary of the Archangel and destroy the hermit St. Archippus. When this feast falls on Sunday, Saturday Vespers joins six Resurrection Stichira with four of the Archangel, with the festal Doxastikon "Rejoice with us, all ye angelic ranks" (*Συγχάρητε ἡμῖν, ἅπασαι αἱ τῶν ἀγγέλων ταξιαρχίαι*), and the Dismissal Troparion of the Bodiless Powers: "Supreme commander of the heavenly hosts, we implore thee..." (*Τῶν οὐρανίων στρατιῶν Ἀρχιστράτηγε*, Tone 4).
[^142]: The Forefeast of the Nativity of the Theotokos and the Holy Martyr Sozon (Violakis, pp. 154–155, September 7, §§1–3). September 7 commemorates the Forefeast (*Προεόρτια*) of the Nativity of the Most Holy Mother of God, joined with the commemoration of the Holy Martyr Sozon of Lycaonia/Cilicia (martyred c. 304 AD under Maximian). When September 7 occurs on the Lord's Day, it coincides with the Sunday before the Exaltation. At Saturday Great Vespers, ten Stichira are chanted at "Lord, I have cried": six of the Resurrection and four Forefeast Idiomela, followed by the Forefeast Doxastikon: "Thy most venerable Nativity, O all-holy Virgin, pure Mother of God, the multitude of angels in heaven and the race of men upon earth do glorify..." (*Τὴν πάνσεπτόν σου Γέννησιν*), and the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichira are concluded by the Forefeast Doxastikon: "The universal joy hath shone forth upon us from the righteous ones, Joachim and Anna..." (*Ἡ παγκόσμιος χαρά*), and the Dismissal Troparia: the Resurrection Troparion and the Forefeast Troparion: "From the root of Jesse and from the loins of David, Mary the child of God is born unto us today..." (*Ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαί*, Tone 4). Violakis notes that the hymnography of the Martyr Sozon is ordinarily relegated to Small Compline; however, if the local temple or parish observes his feast, three stichira of the Saint are intercalated at "Lord, I have cried" and his Troparion is added. At Sunday Matins, two Resurrection Kathismata and one Forefeast Kathisma are sung at each of the two Psalter stichologia. The Canons unite the Sunday Canon and the Forefeast Canon (with the refrain "Most Holy Theotokos, save us"), punctuated by the Katavasiai of the Cross. At the Liturgy, the readings are taken from the Sunday before the Exaltation (Gal. 6:11–18; John 3:13–17).
[^143]: The Nativity of the Most Holy Mother of God, September 8: Festal Rank, Vigil, and Typikon Synthesis (Violakis, pp. 156–157, September 8, §§4–5). The Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos (*Τὸ Γενέσιον τῆς Ὑπεραγίας Θεοτόκου*) on September 8 is the first of the Twelve Great Feasts of the Byzantine ecclesiastical liturgical year, commemorating the birth of the Virgin Mary to the righteous ancestors of God Joachim and Anna in fulfillment of ancestral prophecies. Under the patriarchal reform of George Violakis, the feast is ranked among the great feasts of the Mother of God celebrated with Great Vespers, Litē (*Λιτή*), and festive Matins. When celebrated on a weekday, Great Vespers appoints the First Stasis of the First Kathisma of the Psalter (*Blessed is the man*, Psalm 1 LXX), followed at "Lord, I have cried" by six Idiomela Stichira in Tone 6 composed by St. Sergius of Jerusalem and St. Stephen the Sabaite, doubled with "Glory... Both now...". The three Old Testament lessons (Genesis 28:10–17, Jacob's ladder; Ezekiel 43:27–44:4, the shut gate seen by the prophet; Proverbs 9:1–11, Wisdom hath builded Her house) provide the primary typological framework for Marian veneration in the Byzantine rite. At Matins, the celebration incorporates the Midnight Office, the Festal Litē, and the Polyeleos taken from Psalm 44 LXX (*Ἐξηρεύξατο ἡ καρδία μου λόγον ἀγαθόν*, "My heart overfloweth with a good word"), which constitutes the royal epithalamium typifying the Mother of God as the Queen seated at the King's right hand. Following the Anavathmoi (Tone 4, Antiphon 1) and the Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX), the Matins Gospel is Luke 1:39–49, 56 (the Visitation of Mary to Elizabeth and the Magnificat), followed by the post-Gospel Idiomelon in Tone 2 (*Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα Κυρίου*). The hymnography features two canons: the First Canon composed by St. John of Damascus (Tone 2, Heirmos: *Δεῦτε λαοί*) and the Second Canon composed by St. Andrew of Crete (Tone 8, Heirmos: *Ἁρματηλάτην Φαραώ*), punctuated by the Katavasiai of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*). At Ode 9, the biblical canticles give way to the proper festal megalynaria and the Ninth Ode Heirmos (*Μυστικὸς εἶ Θεοτόκε*).
[^144]: The Divine Liturgy of the Nativity of the Theotokos: Proper Festal Antiphons and Zadostoinyk (Violakis, pp. 158–159, September 8, §6). On the Feast of the Nativity of the Theotokos, the Divine Liturgy replaces the ordinary weekday psalms and Typika with three proper Festal Antiphons derived primarily from Psalm 131 LXX and Psalm 45 LXX. The first antiphon incorporates verses emphasizing David's vow to build a sanctuary for God (Psalm 131:1, 6; Psalm 86:3; Psalm 45:6 LXX) with the Marian refrain: "Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, O Savior, save us." The second antiphon presents the messianic oath made unto David regarding the royal heir to his eternal throne (Psalm 131:11, 17, 13 LXX) with the christological refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art wonderful in the saints, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!" (which in Ruthenian and Slavic practice is alternatively rendered: "Who art wonderful in the saints" or "Through the prayers of the Theotokos"). The third antiphon proclaims the eternal habitation of God in Sion (Psalm 131:14; Psalm 45:5; Psalm 64:5 LXX), interspersed with the festal Dismissal Troparion: "Thy Nativity, O Theotokos Virgin..." (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου Θεοτόκε*, Tone 4). At the Little Entrance, the clergy and choirs chant the festal Entrance Verse: "O come, let us worship and bow down before Christ: Save us, O Son of God, Who art wonderful in the saints, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!". In place of the ordinary Marian hymn *Axion Estin*, the Liturgy appoints the Zadostoinyk (*Ἀντὶ τοῦ Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), consisting of the festal megalynarion and the Heirmos of the Ninth Ode of the Second Canon (Tone 8): "Virginity is foreign to mothers, and childbearing strange to virgins; yet in thee, O Theotokos, both were accomplished: wherefore all we generations of the earth unceasingly magnify thee" (*Ἀλλότριον τῶν μητέρων ἡ παρθενία*). The Communion Verse is Psalm 115:4 LXX: "I will take the cup of salvation, and I will call upon the name of the Lord. Alleluia" (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι*).
[^145]: Sunday Concurrence with the Nativity of the Theotokos and Precedence of the Sunday before the Exaltation (Violakis, pp. 160–161, September 8, §§7–9). When September 8 falls on the Lord's Day, a complex liturgical concurrence occurs between the Resurrectional service of the prevailing Octoechos Tone, the Feast of the Nativity of the Theotokos, and the Sunday before the Exaltation of the Precious Cross (*Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῆς Ὑψώσεως*). At Saturday Great Vespers, the ten Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" are divided: four of the Resurrection and six Idiomela of the Feast, with the festal Doxastikon (*Σήμερον ὁ τοῖς νοεροῖς θρόνοις*) chanted at "Glory... Both now...". The Old Testament readings of the Feast are retained. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichira take precedence, concluded by the festal Doxastikon: "Come, all ye faithful" (*Δεῦτε ἅπαντες πιστοί*). At Matins, the Polyeleos of the Feast is appended to the Psalter Kathismata, and the Sunday Anavathmoi are followed by the festal Prokeimenon and the festal Matins Gospel (Luke 1:39–49, 56). The Sunday chant *Anastasin Christou theasamenoi* is sung, followed by the festal Idiomelon at Psalm 50. In the hymnographic canon, the Resurrection Canon precedes both Canons of the Feast, and the Katavasiai remain those of the Precious Cross (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*). At the Divine Liturgy, the proper Festal Antiphons are sung with the Sunday second-antiphon refrain: "Save us, O Son of God, Who art risen from the dead...". Crucially, Violakis specifies that the Epistle (Galatians 6:11–18: "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ") and the Gospel (John 3:13–17: "No man hath ascended up to heaven, but He that came down from heaven...") are taken exclusively from the Sunday before the Exaltation, while the Zadostoinyk and Communion Verse remain those of the Nativity of the Theotokos.
[^146]: Commemoration of the Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God Joachim and Anna on Sunday and Afterfeast Progression (Violakis, pp. 162–163, September 9, §§10–13). September 9 observes the Synaxis of the Holy and Righteous Ancestors of God Joachim and Anna (*Σύναξις τῶν ἁγίων καὶ δικαίων Θεοπατόρων Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννης*), celebrating the parents of the Mother of God on the day following her Nativity, according to the ancient patristic principle whereby the primary human instruments of a divine mystery are venerated on the morrow of the feast. On weekdays, their office is joined directly with the hymns of the Afterfeast from the Menaion. When September 9 coincides with Sunday (§§10–12), the service of the Lord's Day combines six Resurrection Stichira with four of the Ancestors of God (*Δεῦτε νῦν χορεύσωμεν*), crowned by their Doxastikon: "O blessed couple, Joachim and Anna" (*Ὦ μακαρία δυάς*), and the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichira are sealed by the Doxastikon of the Saints: "They who from barren loins" (*Οἱ ἐξ ἀκάρπων λαγόνων*), and the Dismissal Troparia include the Resurrection Troparion, the Troparion of the Saints (*Οἱ ἐν χάριτι δικαιωθέντες* or their proper dismissal troparion), and the festal Troparion of the Nativity. At Matins, the Kathismata of the Feast replace the ordinary Theotokia, and the Canons join the Resurrection Canon with the Canon of the Saints, sealed by the Katavasiai of the Cross. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes combine four of the Tone and four from Ode 6 of the Canon of the Saints, and the readings are those of the Sunday before the Exaltation. Paragraph 13 establishes the general rubric for the "Sunday after the Feast" (*Κυριακὴ μετὰ τὴν ἑορτήν*), when the Afterfeast continues through September 12.
[^147]: The Apodosis of the Nativity of the Theotokos on Weekdays and Sunday (Violakis, pp. 164–165, September 12, §§15–17). The liturgical cycle of the Nativity of the Theotokos culminates on September 12 with its Apodosis (*Ἀπόδοσις*), concluding the four-day Afterfeast period prior to the inauguration of the Forefeast of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious Cross on September 13. When the Apodosis falls on a weekday (§15), the entire service of September 8 is repeated verbatim with specific omissions reflecting its non-initiatory character: at Vespers, the Kathisma of the Psalter and the three Old Testament readings are omitted; at Matins, the Litē, the Polyeleos, and the festal Matins Gospel are omitted, while the full festal canons, Katavasiai, and praises are sung; at the Divine Liturgy, the festal antiphons and Zadostoinyk are repeated, but the Epistle and Gospel are appointed from the regular weekday cycle. When the Apodosis coincides with Sunday (§§16–17), it merges with the Sunday before the Exaltation. At Saturday Great Vespers, four Resurrection Stichira combine with six of the Feast, and the Aposticha join the Resurrection stichira with the festal aposticha. At Sunday Matins, the Resurrection Kathismata are intercalated with those of the Feast, the Canons combine the Resurrection and the Feast, and the Katavasiai of the Cross are chanted. The Liturgy unites the Sunday Beatitudes with Ode 6 of the Feast, the Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday before the Exaltation, and the Zadostoinyk and festal Communion Verse of the Nativity.
[^148]: Feast of the Consecration of the Temple of the Holy Resurrection in Jerusalem and Forefeast of the Holy Cross on Sunday (Violakis, pp. 166–169, September 13, §§1–4). September 13 commemorates the Dedication or Consecration (*Ἐγκαίνια*) of the Church of the Holy Sepulchre (the Temple of the Resurrection, *Ἀνάστασις*) in Jerusalem, constructed under the Emperor Saint Constantine the Great and consecrated in A.D. 335. In Byzantine liturgical theology, this feast serves as the historical and liturgical threshold for the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross on the following day (September 14), since the Holy Cross was first solemnly displayed and exalted before the assembled Christian multitude on the morrow of this very consecration. The day is also observed as the Forefeast (*Προεόρτια*) of the Precious Cross and commemorates the Holy Hieromartyr Cornelius the Centurion. When September 13 concurs with the Lord's Day (§§2–4), the office combines the Sunday Resurrectional order with the festal propers of the Consecration and the Forefeast. At Saturday Great Vespers, the ten Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" are partitioned into four of the Resurrection, three of the Consecration, and three of the Forefeast taken from Small Vespers (*Ὑψουμένου σου Δέσποτα*), crowned by the Doxastikon of the Consecration (*Τὴν μνήμην τῶν Ἐγκαινίων*) and the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone. The Old Testament readings of the Consecration (1 Kings 8:22–30, the dedication prayer of Solomon; Proverbs 3:19–34, the establishment of the earth by Wisdom; Proverbs 9:1–11, Wisdom hath builded Her house) reflect the christological fulfillment of the temple in the Body of Christ and the Church. At Matins, the Triadic Canon and hymns precede the dismissal troparia: the Resurrection Troparion, the Troparion of the Consecration (*Ὡς τοῦ ἄνω στερεώματος*), and the Forefeast Troparion (*Τὸν ζωοποιὸν Σταυρὸν τῆς σῆς ἀγαθότητος*). The hymnographic canon combines the Resurrection Canon with the Canon of the Cross (Tone 4, by St. Cosmas of Maiuma) and the Canon of the Consecration (Tone 4, by St. John of Damascus), punctuated by the Katavasiai of the Holy Cross (*Σταυρὸν χαράξας*). At the Divine Liturgy, the Beatitudes combine four of the Tone with four from Ode 6 of the Canon of the Consecration; the Epistle (Galatians 6:11–18) and Gospel (John 3:13–17) are taken from the Sunday before the Exaltation, while the Zadostoinyk remains the ordinary *Axion Estin*.
[^149]: Translation and Commemoration of St. John Chrysostom on the Feast of the Universal Exaltation of the Precious Cross (Violakis, pp. 168–169, September 14, Rubrical Note). Historically, Saint John Chrysostom, Archbishop of Constantinople and Doctor of the Universal Church, fell asleep in the Lord on September 14, A.D. 407, at Comana in Pontus during his second exile. Because September 14 is dedicated entirely to the Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross—a feast ranking as a Great Feast of the Lord which completely absorbs all other commemorations—the liturgical constitution of the Byzantine rite transfers the liturgical celebration of Saint John Chrysostom to November 13. The rubrical note in the Violakis Typikon explicitly records that this transfer was instituted precisely so that the hymns, readings, and liturgical praises of Saint John Chrysostom might remain complete, intact, and undiminished (*ἀνελλιπῆ καὶ ἀμείωτα*), without being displaced or curtailed by the festal hegemony of the Exaltation. This principle reflects the traditional Byzantine typikon jurisprudence regarding feast day displacement and ensures the full commemoration of both the Precious Cross and the universal hierarch.
[^150]: Sunday Precedence, Festal Absorption, and the Liturgical Rite of the Procession of the Holy Cross at Matins (Violakis, pp. 170–171, September 14, §§5–6). The Universal Exaltation of the Precious and Life-Creating Cross on September 14 constitutes one of the Twelve Great Feasts of the Lord (*Δεσποτικαὶ ἑορταί*). When September 14 coincides with the Lord's Day (§5), an exceptional rule of festal absorption governs the services: the entire Sunday Resurrectional office is superseded and eliminated, and the festal propers of the Holy Cross are chanted exclusively (*οὐδὲν τῶν Ἀναστασίμων ψάλλομεν, ἀλλ’ ἅπαντα τὰ τῆς ἑορτῆς*). Only two elements of Sunday character are retained: the chant *Anastasin Christou theasamenoi* ("Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ") at Matins, which is uniquely appointed to be chanted on the Exaltation regardless of the day of the week on which the feast falls, signifying the indissoluble bond between the Cross and the Resurrection; and the Matins Gospel reading (John 12:28–36), read from the Royal Doors. At the conclusion of the Great Doxology, during the slow and ornate chanting of the Asmatikon Trisagion (*Ἅγιος ὁ Θεός*), the solemn liturgical Procession of the Precious Cross takes place. The officiating priest, having censed the Cross on the Holy Table where it rests on a tray amidst sprigs of sweet basil and three lighted candles, lifts the tray upon his head. Preceded by lighted tapers, the six-winged liturgical fans (*Exapteryga*), the chanters, and the Primikyrios bearing the two-wicked candle (*Didamvulon*), the priest circles the Holy Table from right to left (counter-clockwise) and carries the Cross through the Holy Doors to the center of the temple. There, circling the adorned Tetrapod three times, he stops facing East, elevates the tray, proclaims the liturgical cry *Sophia, orthoi!* ("Wisdom! Let us attend!"), and deposits the Cross upon the Tetrapod for the ceremony of the Elevation.
[^151]: The Solemn Rite of the Fivefold Elevation of the Holy Cross with Five Hundred Kyrie Eleisons (Violakis, pp. 172–173, September 14, §6 continued).
