In this occurrence, the dominical Resurrection office is combined with both the Fathers and the Forefeast of the Nativity (which commences on December 20). At Saturday Great Vespers (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 4 Resurrection Stichira are joined with 3 Forefeast Prosomoia (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ* / "O all-blameless Virgin of God") and 3 of the Fathers (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί* / "Today, ye faithful, let us celebrate the memory of the Fathers"), concluding at "Glory" with the Doxastikon in Tone 6 *Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν* ("Daniel, a man of desires") and at "Both now and ever" with the First Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; three Old Testament composite readings of the Fathers are read (Genesis 14:14–20; Deuteronomy 1:8–11, 15–17; Deuteronomy 10:14–21); at the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichira conclude at "Glory" with *Χαίρετε, προφῆται τίμιοι* ("Rejoice, ye honored Prophets") and at "Both now and ever" with the Forefeast Theotokion *Ἰδοὺ καιρὸς ἤγγικε* ("Behold, the time is at hand"); and the Dismissal Troparia combine the Resurrection, the Fathers (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*), and the Forefeast (*Ἑτοιμάζου Βηθλεέμ*). At Sunday Matins (§ 5), after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon is followed at the Lite by "Glory": *Βολίδες ἀστράπτοντες* ("Flashing like lightning bolts") and "Both now and ever": *Ἄκουε οὐρανέ* ("Hear, O heaven"); at the Kathismata following the Polyeleos, two Resurrection Kathismata are joined with one Forefeast Kathisma (*Τῶν προφητῶν αἱ ῥήσεις* / "The sayings of the Prophets") at the first stichologia, and two Resurrection with another Forefeast Kathisma (*Αὐλῶν ποιμενικῶν* / "While shepherds were piping") at the second stichologia; the Canon is the Menaion Canon of the Fathers (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*); after Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον* and Resurrection Kontakion are recited; after Ode 6, the Forefeast Kontakion *Εὐφραίνου Βηθλεέμ* ("Be glad, O Bethlehem") and Ikos *Τῆς σῆς, Παρθένε, κυήσεως* ("Of Thy conception, O Virgin") are chanted with the dual Synaxarion; and at the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichira are combined with 4 of the Fathers. Leaf p272 concludes mid-sentence at § 6 ("After the Little Entrance,"), resolving on physical leaf p273.
[^196]: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ (Case 2 Concluded & Case 3: December 24 Eve Concurrence). Physical leaf p273 (printed page 258) and facing English leaf p274 (printed page 259) complete the Eucharistic Liturgy of Case 2 (§ 6), specifying the entrance Apolytikia (Resurrection, Forefeast, Fathers, Temple Patron), the Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον* ("Today the Virgin cometh unto the cave"), and the appointed Epistle (Hebrews 11:9–10, 32–40) and Gospel (Matthew 1:1–25). The text then articulates Case 3 (§§ 7–8): when the Sunday before the Nativity falls on December 24 itself (the Paramony / Eve of the Nativity). Here Violakis formulates a crucial liturgical exception: because December 24 is the final and most intensive day of the Forefeast, the dominical Resurrection hymns are entirely suppressed at Saturday Great Vespers (§ 7), and the service is sung exclusively from the Menaion for the Fathers and the Forefeast. At "Lord, I have cried", 4 Prosomoia of the Fathers (*Τὰ τῶν Πατέρων σήμερον πιστοί*) are combined with 4 of the Forefeast (*Προεορτάσωμεν λαοὶ Χριστοῦ τὰ γενέθλια* / "Let us celebrate beforehand, O ye peoples, the Nativity of Christ", transferred from Dec 20); at "Glory": *Δανιὴλ ἀνὴρ ἐπιθυμιῶν*; at "Both now and ever": *Σπήλαιον εὐτρεπίζου* ("Prepare thyself, O cave"); at the Aposticha, 3 Forefeast Prosomoia (*Παρθένε πανάμωμε Θεοῦ*) are chanted with Habakkuk psalm verses (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἀπὸ Θαιμὰν ἥξει* / "God shall come from Teman" and *Κύριε, εἰσακήκοα τὴν ἀκοήν σου* / "O Lord, I have heard Thy report"); and the Dismissal Troparia are those of the Fathers (*Μεγάλα τὰ τῆς πίστεως κατορθώματα*) and the Forefeast (*Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* / "Mary once, with aged Joseph, went to be enrolled"). At Sunday Matins (§ 8), instead of the Triadic Canon after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Canon *Κύματι θαλάσσης* appointed after Vespers of the 24th is sung; at "God is the Lord", the Resurrection Dismissal Troparion is restored alongside those of the Fathers and Forefeast; and the Kathismata integrate the Resurrection with Forefeast hymnography. Leaf p274 concludes mid-sentence at "then the Litany and the Hypakoe of the Tone, the...", resolving on physical leaf p275.
[^197]: Sunday before the Nativity Concluded (Case 3, §§ 8–9) and Feast of the Nativity of Christ (December 25, Case 1: Friday Occurrence, §§ 1–2). Physical leaf p275 (printed page 260) and facing English leaf p276 (printed page 261) complete Case 3 of the Sunday before the Nativity. At Sunday Matins (§ 8 concl.), two canons are combined: the Canon of the Fathers (*Κύματι θαλάσσης*) and the Forefeast Canon (*Χριστὸν σαρκὶ νηπιάσαντα* / "Christ being an infant in the flesh"); after Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ἄγγελος Παίδων ἐδρόσισε κάμινον* is recited; after Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Three Children (*Χειρόγραφον εἰκόνα μὴ σεβασθέντες* / "Refusing to worship the graven image") and Ikos (*Ἔκτεινόν σου τὴν χεῖρα* / "Stretch out Thy hand") are chanted; and at the Praises, 4 Resurrection Stichira are joined with 4 Troparia of the Fathers (*Ἆρόν σου τὴν φωνὴν ἀληθῶς* / "In truth lift up thy voice, O Zion"). In the Divine Liturgy (§ 9), the Beatitudes combine Troparia from Ode 3 of the Fathers' Canon and Ode 6 of the Forefeast Canon. The Typikon then opens the solemn Feast of the Nativity according to the Flesh of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ (December 25). Case 1 (§ 1) governs when the Feast of the Nativity occurs on a Friday. In this occurrence, Thursday (December 24) is the Paramony (Eve): in the morning, following daily Matins, the Great Hours (Royal Hours: First, Third, Sixth, and Ninth) are chanted, immediately followed by Great Vespers joined with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. [^198]: Feast of the Nativity of Christ: The Royal Hours (First Hour Concluded & Third Hour, §§ 2–3). Physical leaf p277 (printed page 262) and facing English leaf p278 (printed page 263) provide the ceremonial ordotikon for the First and Third Royal Hours of the Nativity Eve when the Feast falls on Friday. At the First Hour (§ 2 concl.), the Patriarch or presiding Hierarch descends into the nave and begins the opening blessing (*Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν... Βασιλεῦ Οὐράνιε...*); three special psalms are read (Psalms 5, 44, and 45 LXX); following the Troparion *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* and Theotokion, three idiomela are chanted antiphonally by the two choirs (*Βηθλεὲμ ἑτοιμάζου*, *Νῦν προφητικὴ πρόρρησις*, and *Τάδε λέγει Ἰωσήφ*); the First Canonarch reads the Prophecy (Micah 5:2–4, prophesying the birth in Bethlehem Ephrathah) and the Epistle (Hebrews 1:1–12, proclaiming the divine Sonship of Christ superior to the angels); and the Priest proclaims the Holy Gospel (Matthew 1:18–25, the Virginal Conception and birth of Emmanuel) before the Holy Doors. In an important rubrical note, Violakis specifies that during the chanting of the idiomela of the Third Hour, the Great Archdeacon (or Deacon, or Priest who read the Gospel) comes forth from the North Door dressed in a black mandyas, bearing a katzion (hand-censer with bells) preceded by a taper-bearer (Lambadouchos), and censes the people, a ceremony repeated at the Sixth and Ninth Hours by other deacons (in the absence of a Hierarch, the Priest censes robed in a phelonion). At the Third Hour (§ 3), following the psalms (Psalms 28, 66, and 50 LXX) and the Troparion of the Forefeast, the choirs chant the idiomela *Οὗτος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν* ("This is our God"), *Πρὸ τῆς γεννήσεως τῆς σῆς* ("Before Thy birth, O Lord"), and *Ἰωσὴφ εἰπὲ ἡμῖν* ("Tell us, Joseph"). Leaf p278 breaks off mid-sentence at "Then the...", resolving on physical leaf p279.
[^199]: Feast of the Nativity of Christ: The Royal Hours Concluded (Third Hour Concl., Sixth and Ninth Hours, §§ 3–5). Physical leaf p279 (printed page 264) and facing English leaf p280 (printed page 265) conclude the Royal Hours of the Nativity. At the Third Hour (§ 3 concl.), the Second Canonarch proclaims the Prophecy (Baruch 3:35–4:4, Christ appearing upon earth and conversing with men) and the Epistle (Galatians 3:23–29, the Law as tutor unto Christ, and adoption as sons through faith), and the Priest reads the Gospel (Luke 2:1–20, the Caesar Augustus census, the manger, and the Angelic Gloria heard by the shepherds). At the Sixth Hour (§ 4), after Psalms 71, 131, and 90 LXX, the idiomela are *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπαρθῶμεν ἐνθέως* ("Come, ye faithful, let us be inspired divinely"), *Ἄκουε, οὐρανέ* ("Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth"), and *Δεῦτε, χριστοφόροι λαοί* ("Come, ye Christ-bearing peoples"); the Prophecy is Isaiah 7:10–16; 8:1–4, 9–10 (the virgin conceiving Emmanuel), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:11–18 (Christ partaking of flesh and blood to destroy the devil), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:1–12 (the Adoration of the Magi). At the Ninth Hour (§ 5), after Psalms 109, 110, and 85 LXX, the idiomela are *Ἐξεπλήττετο ὁ Ἡρώδης* ("Herod was struck with amazement") and *Ὅτε Ἰωσήφ, Παρθένε* ("When Joseph, O Virgin"); then the Canonarch stands in the midst of the nave facing east and solemnly chants the celebrated idiomelon *Σήμερον γεννᾶται ἐκ Παρθένου ὁ δρακὶ τὴν πᾶσαν ἔχων κτίσιν* ("Today He Who holds all creation in the hollow of His hand is born of a Virgin") in Gospel recitative style thrice, continuing with the strophes, repeating thrice *Προσκυνοῦμέν σου τὴν γέννησιν, Χριστέ* ("We worship Thy Nativity, O Christ"), and once *Δεῖξον ἡμῖν καὶ τὰ θεῖά σου Θεοφάνεια* ("Show us also Thy divine Theophany"), whereupon the choirs repeat the idiomelon melodiously; the Prophecy is Isaiah 9:6–7 (Unto us a Child is born), the Epistle is Hebrews 2:1–10 (Jesus crowned with glory and honor), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:13–23 (the Flight into Egypt and Slaughter of the Holy Innocents). In Note 3, Violakis explains that historically the Typika were read after the Ninth Hour, but in modern practice are omitted to transition directly to Great Vespers with the Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.

Note 4 clarifies that after communion, the Troparion of the Feast (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου, Χριστὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*) is chanted instead of *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς* ("We have seen the true light"), because Vespers has concluded. Matins (§ 7) opens at the early dawn; at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Feast is chanted thrice.

Who art risen from the dead"; the Baptismal hymn *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστόν* ("As many of you as have been baptized into Christ", Galatians 3:27) replaces the Trisagion; the Epistle (Galatians 1:11–19) and Gospel (Matthew 2:13–23) are of the Sunday after Nativity; Megalynarion is the Heirmos of Ode 9 (*Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*); Communion Verse is Psalm 110:9 LXX (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε* / "The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"). Paragraph 21 assigns the Apodosis to Friday, December 31. Paragraph 22 introduces Situation Three (Γ΄), where December 25 falls on Sunday: on Friday morning, the Royal Hours alone are sung without Divine Liturgy, using the Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ* ("Prepare, Bethlehem"), since *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* ("Mary was registered once in a census") is reserved for the immediate Paramony.
[^208]: Situation Three Continued: Friday Evening Forefeast Vespers (§ 23); Saturday Paramony Matins and Liturgy (§ 24); Saturday Evening Great Festal Vespers (§ 25); Sunday Festal Matins and Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (§ 26); Transfer of Sunday after the Nativity to Monday (§ 26 note). Physical leaf p297 (printed page 282) and facing English leaf p298 (printed page 283) continue Situation Three (Nativity on Sunday). On Friday evening (§ 23), daily Vespers is sung from the Menaion, followed after *Νῦν ἀπολύεις* by the Forefeast Canon (*Κύματι θαλάσσης* / "Waves of the sea") and the Forefeast Dismissal Troparion *Ἀπεγράφετό ποτε* ("Mary was registered once in a census"). On Saturday morning (§ 24), Matins is sung with Canons read plain, Heirmos of Ode 8 chanted, Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*), Forefeast Exapostilaria, and Praises (*Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν* / "What mysteries beyond understanding"); Divine Liturgy features the daily Antiphons (*Ἀγαθὸν τὸ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι* / "It is good to give praise unto the Lord", Psalm 91:2 LXX), Entrance Hymn *ὁ ἐν ἁγίοις θαυμαστός* ("Who art wondrous in Thy saints"), Forefeast Dismissal Troparion, Epistle and Gospel of the Saturday before the Nativity, and Communion Verse Psalm 64:5 LXX (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω* / "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"). On Saturday evening (§ 25), Great Festal Vespers of the Nativity is chanted with 6 Stichira Idiomela (*Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*), Gospel Entrance, 8 Old Testament Readings, and immediately following the 8th reading (without the Litany) the Epistle and Gospel are proclaimed; then the Augmented Litany, Aposticha Idiomela (*Μέγα καὶ παράδοξον θαῦμα*), and Festal Dismissal Troparion thrice. On Sunday (§ 26), Festal Matins and the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great are celebrated as in Situation One. The concluding note explains that because the solitary Sunday between Nativity and Theophany coincides with January 1 (Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great), the commemoration of the Sunday after the Nativity (the Holy Ancestors of God) is transferred and joined to the Synaxis of the Theotokos on Monday, December 26.
[^209]: Combined Celebration of the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos and Sunday after the Nativity (Ancestors of God) on Monday, December 26 (§§ 27–29). Physical leaf p299 (printed page 284) and facing English leaf p300 (printed page 285) provide the complete ordotikon for the joint celebration on Monday, December 26, when Nativity falls on Sunday. On Sunday evening (§ 27), Vespers features 6 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" (3 Festal Idiomela *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα* and 3 of the Ancestors of God *Δεῦτε συμφώνως ἅπαντες Δαυῒδ τὸν ἀοίδιμον* / "Come, let us extol David the king"), Doxastikon of the Ancestors (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*), Theotokion (*Δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις Θεῷ*), Entrance with Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7 (*Τίς Θεὸς μέγας*, Psalm 76:14 LXX), Festal Aposticha (*Παράδοξον μυστήριον*), and Dismissal Troparia of the Nativity and the Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*). At Monday Matins (§ 28), following the Hexapsalmos, "God is the Lord", and Festal Kathismata (*Δεῦτε ἴδωμεν, πιστοί* and *Τί θαυμάζεις, Μαριάμ;*), Psalm 50 [LXX] is read plain without Polyeleos; Canons combine the Nativity First Canon (*Χριστὸς γεννᾶται*) and that of the Betrothed (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*); after Ode 3, Kathismata *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς* and *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*; after Ode 6, Kontakion, Ikos, and Synaxarion of the Ancestors; Ode 9 is chanted with the Festal Megalynaria and Katavasia *Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*; Exapostilaria of the Ancestors (*Σὺν Ἰακώβῳ μέλψωμεν*) and the Feast (*Ἐπεσκέψατο ἡμᾶς*); Praises with 4 Festal Stichira (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*), Doxastikon (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*), and Great Doxology. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 29), the Festal Antiphons are sung as on the feast; Entrance Verse is Psalm 109:3 LXX (*Ἐκ γαστρὸς πρὸ Ἑωσφόρου*); Dismissal Troparia of the Nativity, the Ancestors, and Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν ὑπερούσιον τίκτει*; Baptismal hymn *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστόν* replaces the Trisagion; Epistle and Gospel are of the Sunday after the Nativity; Megalynarion is the Heirmos *Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*; and Communion Verse is Psalm 110:9 LXX (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε* / "The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people").
[^210]: Conclusion of Situation Three (Apodosis date, § 30) and Situation Four: Nativity falling on Monday (§§ 31–35). Physical leaf p301 (printed page 286) and facing English leaf p302 (printed page 287) conclude the rubrics for Situation Three (Γ΄), where December 25 falls on a Sunday. Paragraph 30 assigns the Apodosis of the Feast to the following Saturday. The text notes the print erratum "ἤτοι τῇ Λ΄ τοῦ μηνός" (that is, on the 30th of the month), which is bracketed and corrected to "ὀρθότερον εἶναι τῇ ΛΑ΄ τοῦ μηνός" (more correctly, on the 31st of the month), as December contains 31 days. On this Saturday, the entire festal office is repeated as in Situation One § 15, with the Epistle (1 Timothy 3:13–4:5) and Gospel (Matthew 3:1–11) of the Saturday before Theophany. Situation Four (Δ΄) details the order when December 25 falls on a Monday: on Friday morning (Dec 22, § 31), following Matins, the Royal Hours alone are sung without the Divine Liturgy, following Situation One §§ 1–5; the Dismissal Troparion is *Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ* ("Prepare, Bethlehem"), because the Paramony is separated by the weekend and not immediately adjacent to the Feast (referencing Situation Three § 22). On Friday evening and Saturday morning (Dec 22–23, § 32), the Service of the Ten Holy Martyrs of Crete (Dec 23) is combined with the Forefeast from the Menaion; Dismissal Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου, Βηθλεέμ*, Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον τὸν προαιώνιον Λόγον*; Divine Liturgy includes the Epistle (Galatians 3:8–12) and Gospel (Luke 13:19–29) of the Saturday before the Nativity, and Communion Verse Psalm 64:5 LXX (*Μακάριοι οὓς ἐξελέξω* / "Blessed are they whom Thou hast chosen"). On Saturday evening and Sunday morning (Dec 23–24, § 33), the Sunday before the Nativity (Holy Ancestors) is celebrated as in Situation Three §§ 7–9. On Sunday evening (Dec 24, § 34), Great Festal Vespers is chanted as in Situation Three § 25. On Monday (Dec 25, § 35), Festal Matins is sung as in Situation One §§ 7–8, together with the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great.
[^211]: Situation Four Continued: Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos (§ 36) and Celebration of the Sunday after the Nativity combined with the Apodosis of the Feast (§§ 37–38). Physical leaf p303 (printed page 288) and facing English leaf p304 (printed page 289) continue Situation Four (Nativity on Monday). On Monday evening and Tuesday morning (Dec 25–26, § 36), Vespers, Matins, and Divine Liturgy for the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos are celebrated as prescribed in Situation One §§ 9–10; the Epistle is Hebrews 2:11–18 (*Ὁ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι* / "Both He that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one"), and the Gospel is Matthew 2:13–23 (*Ἀναχωρησάντων τῶν Μάγων* / "And when the wise men had departed"). Paragraphs 37–38 govern the case where the Sunday after the Nativity (Holy Ancestors: David the King, Joseph the Betrothed, and James the Brother of the Lord) coincides with the Apodosis of the Feast on Sunday, December 31. On Saturday evening (§ 37), Great Vespers at "Lord, I have cried" features 10 Stichira (3 Resurrectional, 4 Festal Idiomela *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*, and 3 of the Ancestors of God); "Glory" (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); "Both now and ever" (*Αὐγούστου μοναρχήσαντος*); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha Resurrectional with "Glory" of the Ancestors (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*), "Both now and ever" (*Σπηλαίῳ παρῴκησας*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, of the Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and of the Feast (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*). On Sunday Matins (§ 38), after Psalm 50 [LXX], the Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*) are sung, followed by the Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, and Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Amomos (Kathisma 17 / Psalm 118 LXX); Resurrectional Kathismata with Festal Kathismata instead of Theotokia; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection, of the Feast (*Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*), and of Joseph the Betrothed (*Χριστοῦ θεράπων μακάριε*); after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos plain, Kathisma *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*, "Both now and ever" *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday after the Nativity, Menologion and Synaxarion; double Katavasiai of the Nativity (*Ἔσωσε λαόν* and *Στείβει θαλάσσης*); Morning Gospel order; Ode 9 from both festal canons with their Megalynaria and both Katavasiai of Ode 9; Exapostilaria of the Resurrection, Ancestors, and Feast; Praises with 4 Resurrectional and 4 Festal Stichira; "Glory" (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*), "Both now and ever" (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*), and Great Doxology.
[^212]: Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity and Apodosis (§ 39); Situation Five: Nativity falling on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday (§ 40); and Sunday after the Nativity during the Afterfeast (Saturday Vespers § 41 and Sunday Matins § 42). Physical leaf p305 (printed page 290) and facing English leaf p306 (printed page 291) conclude the Liturgy for Situation Four and open Situation Five (Ε΄). At the Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity and Apodosis (§ 39), the Antiphons of the Feast are sung with the Second Antiphon refrain *Ὁ ἐκ Παρθένου τεχθείς* ("Who wast born of a Virgin"); Entrance Verse of the Feast with the Sunday addition *Ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν* ("Who art risen from the dead"); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Festal (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*), Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), and Temple Patron; Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*; Trisagion Hymn; Epistle (2 Timothy 4:5–8) and Gospel (Mark 1:1–8) of the Sunday before Theophany; at "Especially", the Festal Megalynarion and Heirmos of Ode 9 *Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου . . . Στέργειν μὲν ἡμᾶς*; Communion Verse Psalm 110:9 LXX (*Λύτρωσιν ἀπέστειλε* / "The Lord hath sent redemption unto His people"); Dismissal Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, Dismissal. Situation Five (§ 40) governs Christmas occurring on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday: the Paramony Royal Hours, Great Vespers, and Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, as well as the festal services and the Synaxis of the Theotokos, follow Situation One §§ 1–11. Paragraphs 41–42 detail the celebration of the Sunday after the Nativity when it occurs on an intermediate day of the afterfeast (between Dec 26 and 31). On Saturday evening (§ 41), Great Vespers at "Lord, I have cried" has 10 Stichira (4 Resurrectional, 3 Festal Idiomela *Δεῦτε ἀγαλλιασώμεθα*, 3 of the Ancestors of God); "Glory" (*Μνήμην ἐπιτελοῦμεν*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone (distinct from Situation Four, where the festal Doxastikon is sung); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha Resurrectional with "Glory" of the Ancestors (*Ἱερέων μνήμη*), "Both now and ever" (*Χορεύουσιν Ἄγγελοι*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Ancestors (*Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*), Festal (*Ἡ γέννησίς σου*), Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 42), after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns (*Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*), Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Amomos; Resurrectional Kathismata with afterfeast Kathismata instead of Theotokia; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and of Joseph the Betrothed (the festal canon being omitted here); after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos plain, Kathisma *Πατρὸς ὡς ἀληθῶς*...
[^213]: Situation Five Concluded: Matins and Divine Liturgy of the Sunday after the Nativity (§§ 42 concl., 43); Month of January: January 1, Circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ and Commemoration of Saint Basil the Great (Vespers § 1 and opening of Matins § 2). Physical leaf p307 (printed page 292) and facing English leaf p308 (printed page 293) conclude the five Situations of the Nativity and begin the Month of January. Matins of the Sunday after the Nativity under Situation Five (§ 42 concl.) concludes with Kathisma "Both now and ever" *Χορὸς τῶν Προφητῶν*; after Ode 6: Kontakion of the Sunday after the Nativity (*Εὐφροσύνης σήμερον* / "Of joy today") and Ikos (*Ἀπορρήτῳ βουλῇ* / "By ineffable counsel"), Menologion and Synaxarion; Katavasiai *Ἔσωσε λαόν* (single canon only); Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν* is sung); Exapostilaria of Resurrection, Ancestors, and Feast; Praises with 4 Resurrectional and 4 Festal Stichira (*Εὐφραίνεσθε, δίκαιοι*); "Glory" (*Αἷμα καὶ πῦρ*), "Both now and ever" (*Ὑπερευλογημένη*), Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 43): Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 from Ode 6 of Canon of the Betrothed; Entrance with Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion, *Ἡ γέννησίς σου*, *Εὐαγγελίζου, Ἰωσήφ*, Temple Patron, Kontakion *Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον*; Epistle Galatians 1:11–19, Gospel Matthew 2:13–23; at "Especially": *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν* (normal Megalynarion, since it is an intermediate day and not the Apodosis); Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal. Formal rubric closes: *End of the five Situations of the Feast of the Nativity of Christ.* The Month of January opens on January 1 with the Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great. At Vespers (§ 1): Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], First Stasis of the First Kathisma [Ps. 1–3 LXX]; at "Lord, I have cried", 6 Stichira (2 Festal Idiomela repeating the first, 3 Prosomoia of Saint Basil); "Glory" of the Saint (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); "Both now and ever" (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ*); Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon of the day, 3 Old Testament Readings (Genesis 17:1–14; Proverbs 8:22–30; Proverbs 10:31–11:12); Aposticha: 3 Idiomela of the Saint, "Glory" (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*), "Both now and ever" (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*); Dismissal Troparion of the Saint (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*), then "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Feast once (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and the festal Dismissal (*Ὁ ἐν τῇ ὀγδόῃ ἡμέρᾳ σαρκὶ περιτμηθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν...*). At Matins (§ 2): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Lite of the Saint; Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*, Hexapsalmos.
[^214]: January 1 Matins Concluded (§ 2) and Complete Festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 for the Circumcision of Christ and Saint Basil the Great. Physical leaf p309 (printed page 294) and facing English leaf p310 (printed page 295) conclude Matins for January 1. At "God is the Lord": Dismissal Troparion of Saint Basil twice, and of the Feast once; Psalter of the day and Polyeleos; Kathismata in order; Anavathmoi: First Antiphon of Tone 4 (*Ἐκ νεότητός μου*); Prokeimenon: Violakis notes *Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἐξῆλθεν ὁ φθόγγος αὐτοῦ* [Ps. 18:5 LXX], adding the critical rubrical note that the Menaion and standard liturgical sources indicate *Τὸ στόμα μου λαλήσει σοφίαν* ("My mouth shall speak wisdom", Psalm 48:4 LXX); *Πᾶσα πνοή*; Morning Gospel (John 10:1–9, from November 13); Psalm 50 [LXX] plain; "Glory": *Ταῖς τοῦ Ἱεράρχου*; "Both now and ever": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; Verse Psalm 50:3 LXX (*Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός*); Idiomelon *Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου* (Tone 6); Canon of the Feast *Δεῦτε λαοί* with Verse *Δόξα σοι ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν*, and Canon of Saint Basil *Σοῦ τὴν φωνήν* with Verse *Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*; after Ode 3, Kathismata of Saint Basil and the Feast; after Ode 6, Kontakion and Ikos of Saint Basil, and Menologion; double Katavasiai of Theophany (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* and *Στείβει θαλάσσης*); Ode 9 of both Feast and Saint sung with their respective Megalynaria. The leaf provides the complete text of the Megalynaria for Ode 9: for Canon 1 (Circumcision), 5 refrains (including the Menaion addition in brackets: "Today the Master is circumcised in the flesh, fulfilling the Law as an infant"); and for Canon 2 (Saint Basil), 4 refrains (including the Menaion additions in brackets: "Magnify, O my soul, the most bright luminary of the universe" and "Magnify, O my soul, the adorner of the Church of Christ"). The footnote preserves Violakis's editorial asterisk indicating that these bracketed refrains are commonly chanted in contemporary practice.
[^215]: January 1 (Circumcision of our Lord Jesus Christ and Commemoration of Saint Basil the Great) Continued: Conclusion of Matins Ode 9 Megalynaria, Praises, Great Doxology, and Dismissal; Divine Liturgy Opening and Antiphons 1 and 2 (§ 3). Physical leaf p311 (printed page 296) and facing English leaf p312 (printed page 297) continue the festal office of January 1. At the conclusion of Ode 9 of Matins, the final Megalynaria for the Second Canon (Saint Basil) are chanted: "Glory to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit: Magnify, O my soul, the power of the Godhead in three Persons and undivided"; "Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen: Magnify, O my soul, Her who hath delivered us from the curse." An editorial note preserved in the facsimile indicates that the bracketed Megalynaria marked with asterisks are found in the modern printed Menaion at Ode 9 (Athens: Phos, 1960; Apostoliki Diakonia, 1960/1991), but are not recorded in the classical text of the Violakis Typikon itself or in the rubrical prefaces. Matins concludes with the Exapostilaria of the Saint and the Feast; at the Praises: 4 Prosomoia of Saint Basil, "Glory" (*Ἐξεχύθη ἡ χάρις ἐν χείλεσί σου* / "Grace was poured out upon Thy lips"), "Both now and ever" (*Συγκαταβαίνων ὁ Σωτήρ* / "The Savior, coming down"), Great Doxology, Dismissal Troparion of the Feast (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως* / "In unalterable form"), and Dismissal. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 3), the special festal Antiphons of the Circumcision are appointed: First Antiphon verses from Psalm 65:1 LXX (*᾿Αλαλάξατε τῷ Κυρίῳ πᾶσα ἡ γῆ* / "Make a joyful shout unto the Lord, all the earth!"), Psalm 65:2 LXX (*Ψάλατε δὴ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ* / "Sing praises unto His name"), Psalm 9:2 LXX (*Διηγήσομαι πάντα τὰ θαυμάσιά σου* / "I will tell of all Thy marvelous works"), Psalm 65:3 LXX (*Εἴπατε τῷ Θεῷ· ὡς φοβερὰ τὰ ἔργα σου* / "Say unto God: How awesome are Thy works!"); refrain: *Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου* ("Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"). Second Antiphon verses from Psalm 95:11 LXX (*Εὐφραινέσθωσαν οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ γῆ* / "Let the heavens rejoice and let the earth be glad"), Psalm 97:1 LXX (*῎Ασατε τῷ Κυρίῳ ᾆσμα καινόν* / "Sing unto the Lord a new song"), Psalm 49:2 LXX (*Ἐκ Σιὼν ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος αὐτοῦ* / "Out of Sion is the majesty of His beauty"), Psalm 113:11 LXX (*Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα ὅσα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν* / "Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath willed, He hath done"); refrain: *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ σαρκὶ περιτμηθείς* ("Save us, O Son of God, Who wast circumcised in the flesh, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"), followed by *Ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς* ("Only-begotten Son and Immortal Word of God").
[^216]: January 1 Continued: Third Antiphon, Little Entrance, Troparia, Epistle, Gospel, Liturgy of Saint Basil (§ 3 concl.); and Celebration of the Feast when January 1 falls on a Sunday (Saturday Vespers § 4 and Sunday Matins § 5 opening). Physical leaf p313 (printed page 298) and facing English leaf p314 (printed page 299) conclude the standard weekday order and present the combined Sunday order for January 1. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 3 concl.), the Third Antiphon consists of verses from Psalm 88:2 LXX (*Τὰ ἐλέη σου, Κύριε, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ᾄσομαι* / "Thy mercies, O Lord, will I sing forever"), Psalm 88:3 LXX (*᾿Αναγγελῶ τὴν ἀλήθειάν σου ἐν τῷ στόματί μου* / "With my mouth will I declare Thy truth unto all generations"), Psalm 44:8 LXX (*Ἠγάπησας δικαιοσύνην καὶ ἐμίσησας ἀνομίαν* / "Thou hast loved righteousness and hated iniquity"); refrain: Dismissal Troparion of the Circumcision (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*). At the Little Entrance, the Introit Verse is: *Δεῦτε προσκυνήσωμεν καὶ προσπέσωμεν Χριστῷ· σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ σαρκὶ περιτμηθείς...* ("O come, let us worship and fall down before Christ; save us, O Son of God, Who wast circumcised in the flesh..."). Dismissal Troparia: Circumcision (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), Saint Basil (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*), and Temple Patron; Kontakion of the Circumcision (*Ὁ τῶν ὅλων Κύριος περιτομὴν ὑπομένει* / "The Lord of all endureth circumcision"); Trisagion Hymn; Epistle: Colossians 2:8–12 (*᾿Αδελφοί, βλέπετε μή τις ὑμᾶς ἔσται ὁ συλαγωγῶν* / "Brethren, beware lest any man cheat you"); Gospel: Luke 2:20–21, 40–52 (*Ὑπέστρεψαν οἱ ποιμένες* / "The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God"); Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great; at the Diptychs, the Megalynarion of Saint Basil is chanted (*Τὸν οὐρανοφάντορα τοῦ Χριστοῦ μύστην τοῦ Δεσπότου* / "Let us all extol the great Basil, revealer of heavenly things, initiate of the Master"); Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"); instead of *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*, and Dismissal. Paragraphs 4–5 govern the order when January 1 falls on a Sunday: on Saturday evening (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira are sung (4 Resurrectional, 3 Festal Idiomela repeating the first, and 3 Prosomoia of Saint Basil); "Glory" of Saint Basil (*Σοφίας ἐραστής*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 Old Testament Readings of the Feast; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory" of Saint Basil (*Ὁ τὴν χάριν τῶν θαυμάτων*), "Both now and ever" (*Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη ὁ πανάγαθος Θεός*); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, Saint Basil (*Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν*), Circumcision (*Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*), and Dismissal. On Sunday Matins (§ 5 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Lite of Saint Basil; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Οὐκ ἐπῃσχύνθη*; Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Trisagion Prayers; Troparion *Μορφὴν ἀναλλοιώτως*; Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter and Polyeleos; Kathismata: one Resurrectional, one of Saint Basil, and one of the Feast at the first and second stichologia; at the third stichologia, those of the Menaion in order; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection, Circumcision, and Saint Basil.

The Sunday before Theophany (Κυριακὴ πρὸ τῶν Φώτων), Situation One (§§ 1–2), covers the case when the Sunday occurs on January 2, 3, or 4: on Saturday evening (§ 1), following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and Psalter Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried" 10 Stichira are sung (6 Resurrectional, 4 Forefeast Idiomela from January 2 *Προεόρτια ᾄσματα*); "Glory" (*Ἔρχεται πρὸς Ἰορδάνην* / "He cometh unto Jordan"); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory... On Sunday Matins (§ 2 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon and Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Trisagion Prayers; Dismissal Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου, Ζαβουλών*; Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Resurrectional Dismissal Troparion twice and Forefeast once; Psalter and Amomos (Kathisma 17 / Psalm 118 LXX); Resurrectional Kathismata in order, Evlogitaria...
[^218]: Sunday before Theophany: Situation One Concluded (Matins § 2 concl., Divine Liturgy § 3) and Situation Two: Sunday before Theophany falling on Paramony, January 5 (Saturday Vespers § 4, Sunday Matins § 5 opening). Physical leaf p317 (printed page 302) and facing English leaf p318 (printed page 303) complete Situation One and commence Situation Two. Sunday Matins for Situation One continues (§ 2 concl.) with the Hypakoe of the Tone, Anavathmoi, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and Forefeast; after Ode 3, Kathisma *Ἀόρατε Θεέ* ("Invisible God") once; after Ode 6, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos, Menologion of the day; Katavasiai of Theophany (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*); Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); Exapostilaria: Resurrectional and Forefeast *Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια* ("How shall river streams receive Thee"); Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Forefeast Stichira (*Αἱ ἀγγελικαὶ προπορεύεσθε δυνάμεις* / "O angelic hosts, go before"); "Glory": Morning Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Situation Two (§§ 4–5) applies when the Sunday before Theophany falls on January 5, the Eve (Paramony) of the Feast: on Saturday evening (§ 4), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira are sung (6 Resurrectional, 4 Forefeast Idiomela *Προεόρτια ᾄσματα* [the Greek text contains a print duplication 'Προεόρτια α΄ Προεόρτια ᾄσματα', emended to 4 Forefeast Stichira as witnessed in the English column]); "Glory" (*Ἔρχεται πρὸς Ἰορδάνην*); "Both now and ever": First Theotokion Dogmatikon of the Tone; Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory... On Sunday Matins (§ 5 opening): after Psalm 50 [LXX], Triadic Canon, Triadic hymns *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*, Trisagion Prayers, Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Hexapsalmos; "God is the Lord", Resurrectional Troparion twice, Forefeast once; Psalter and Amomos; Resurrectional Kathismata in order, Evlogitaria, Hypakoe of the Tone, Anavathmoi, Prokeimenon; Canons of the Resurrection and Forefeast (*Χριστὸς μολεῖ πρὸς τὸ βάπτισμα* / "Christ cometh unto baptism") with Verse "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion and Ikos...
[^219]: Sunday before Theophany: Situation Two Concluded (Matins § 5 concl., Divine Liturgy § 6), Great Blessing of the Waters on Paramony; and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Situation One: Feast falling on Friday (Royal Hours on Thursday, Vespers and Liturgy of Saint Basil § 1). Physical leaf p319 (printed page 304) and facing English leaf p320 (printed page 305) conclude the Sunday before Theophany and commence the Feast of the Holy Theophany of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ. Sunday Matins of Situation Two concludes (§ 5 concl.): after Ode 3, Kathisma *Ὁ μέγας ὑετός* ("The great rain" from January 5); after Ode 6, Kontakion of the Forefeast *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*, Ikos, Menologion of the day; Katavasiai *Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα*; Morning Gospel order; Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*); Exapostilaria: Resurrectional and Forefeast *Πῶς ῥεῖθρά σε ποτάμια*; Praises: 4 Resurrectional and 4 Forefeast Stichira (*Ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς* / "Behold the King"); "Glory": Forefeast Doxastikon *Ἰωάννη Βαπτιστά*; "Both now and ever": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 6): Typika and Beatitudes (4 of Tone, 4 from Ode 6 of Forefeast Canon); Entrance with Resurrectional Troparion, Forefeast Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε*, Temple Patron, Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; Epistle (2 Timothy 4:5–8) and Gospel (Mark 1:1–8) of the Sunday before Theophany; at "Especially": *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*. Immediately following the Prayer Behind the Ambon and *Εἴη τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου* ("Blessed be the name of the Lord"), the clergy proceed to the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (Μέγας Ἁγιασμός): the choir chants the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is performed according to the Menaion; Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan") and Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον*; during the blessing and sprinkling of the faithful with holy water, the Second Choir chants the Idiomelon *᾿Ανυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the Dismissal. At the trapeza, wine and olive oil are permitted in honor of the Sunday, relaxing the strict fast otherwise observed on the Eve of Theophany. The Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) opens with Situation One (when January 6 falls on a Friday, § 1): on Thursday morning (January 5), following prescribed Matins, the Royal Hours alone are sung according to the order of the Eve of the Nativity (referencing Christmas Situation One § 2). Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great with the Great Blessing of the Waters at the conclusion of the Liturgy are celebrated on Thursday afternoon according to the prescribed order.
[^220]: Eve of Holy Theophany (January 5) Concluded: Great Vespers Joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great, Old Testament Readings, and Great Blessing of the Waters (§ 2); and Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6): Friday Matins Opening (§ 3). Physical leaf p321 (printed page 306) and facing English leaf p322 (printed page 307) govern the festive eve and opening of Holy Theophany when January 6 falls on a Friday. Great Vespers joined to the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great (§ 2) begins following the Dismissal of the Ninth Hour: the Deacon intones the opening blessing (*Εὐλόγησον, Δέσποτα* / "Bless, Master"), the Priest gives the doxological exclamation *Εὐλογημένη ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Πατρός* ("Blessed is the kingdom of the Father..."), and the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch) reads the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], followed by the Great Litany. At "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: the 4 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν* / "Our illumination") repeating the first two; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Ὑπέκλινας κάραν τῷ Προδρόμῳ* ("Thou hast bowed Thy head unto the Forerunner"). The Little Entrance is made with the Holy Gospel Book, followed by *Φῶς ἱλαρόν* ("O Gladsome Light") and the thirteen Old Testament Readings of the Eve. Following Reading 3 (Genesis 1:1–13: *Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἐποίησεν ὁ Θεός* / "In the beginning God created"), the First Choir intones the Troparion *Ἐπεφάνης ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ* ("Thou hast appeared in the world"), and the Second Choir responds with the choral refrain *Ἵνα φωτίσῃς τοὺς ἐν σκότει καθημένους, Φιλάνθρωπε, δόξα σοι* ("To give light to those who sit in darkness; O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!"), sung alternately between the verses of Psalm 66 LXX until the Canonarch concludes. Following Reading 6 (4 Kingdoms 2:6–14 LXX / 2 Kings 2:6–14: *Εἶπεν Ἠλίας τῷ Ἐλισσαιέ* / "And Elijah said unto Elisha"), the Second Choir intones the Troparion *Ἁμαρτωλοῖς καὶ τελώναις* ("Unto sinners and tax-collectors"), and the choral refrain *Ποῦ γὰρ εἶχε τὸ φῶς σου λάμψαι* ("Where indeed should Thy light have shone...") is alternated between the verses of Psalm 92 LXX. Following Reading 13 (4 Kingdoms 5:1–14 LXX / 2 Kings 5:1–14: *Παραγένετο Νεεμὰν βασιλέως Ἀσσυρίων* / "So Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria [printed Ἀσσυρίων]"), the Small Litany is intoned, the Trisagion Hymn is chanted, followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 9:19–27), "Alleluia", and the Holy Gospel (Luke 3:1–18) proclaimed from the ambo, followed by the Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great. The Communion Verse is Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"), followed by *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν* ("We have seen the true light"). After the Prayer behind the Ambon, the clergy proceed to the solea for the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters (*Μέγας Ἁγιασμός*): the choirs chant the Idiomela *Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* ("The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), and the office is celebrated according to the Menaion; during the sprinkling of the faithful, the Second Choir sings the Idiomelon *Ἀνυμνήσωμεν οἱ πιστοί* ("Let us, the faithful, praise"), followed by the solemn festal Dismissal with its proper characteristic incipit: *Ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν, Χριστὸς ὁ ἀληθινὸς Θεὸς ἡμῶν* ("May He Who deigned to be baptized by John in the Jordan for our salvation, Christ our true God..."). The rubrics prescribe xerophagy (*ξηροφαγία*, strict fast without wine or oil) at table on this eve. Paragraph 3 opens Friday Matins for the feast: following Psalm 50 [LXX], the Lite and the Idiomela of the Aposticha (omitted on the eve due to the vigil Liturgy) are chanted; then the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), and the Hexapsalmos; at "God is the Lord", the Dismissal Troparion is chanted thrice, followed by the Psalter Kathismata and the festal Polyeleos (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου*, Psalm 134 LXX; the printed English column incorrectly labels this Psalm 135 LXX by confusing Masoretic numbering).
[^221]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Friday Matins Gospel Order, Canons, and Festive Megalynaria of the Ninth Ode (§ 3 cont.). Physical leaf p323 (printed page 308) and facing English leaf p324 (printed page 309) provide the rubrical sequence of Friday Matins from the Kathismata through the Ninth Ode. Following the 3 Kathisma sedalia, the Anavathmoi of Tone 4 (First Antiphon *Ἐκ νεότητός μου* / "From my youth") are sung, followed by the Prokeimenon from Psalm 113:3 LXX (*Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν, ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled, Jordan was driven back"). After *Πᾶσα πνοὴ αἰνεσάτω τὸν Κύριον* ("Let everything that hath breath praise the Lord"), the Matins Gospel is proclaimed (Mark 1:9–11), followed by Psalm 50 [LXX] read simply; "Glory": *Τὰ σύμπαντα σήμερον ἀγαλλιάσθω* ("Today let all things greatly rejoice"); "Both now and ever": the same; Verse: *Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ Θεός* (Ps. 50:3 LXX) and the Idiomelon *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Both Canons of the Feast are chanted with 4 troparia each, without verses except for "Glory... Both now and ever..." in each Ode: the First Canon by Saint Cosmas the Melodist in Tone 2 (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* / "He uncovered the bottom of the deep") and the Second Iambic Canon by Saint John Damascene in Tone 2 (*Στείβει θαλάσσης* / "The Lord, working wonders"). After Ode 3, the Hypakoe *Ὅτε τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ σου* ("When at Thy manifestation"); after Ode 6, the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"), the Ikos, and the Menologion. Both Katavasiai are sung in full at each Ode. At Ode 9, the Magnificat (*Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*) is not sung; instead, the festive Megalynaria (*Μεγαλυνάρια*) are appointed for each troparion. For the First Canon, four primary Megalynaria are given: (1) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν τιμιωτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable than the heavenly hosts"); (2) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ἐλθόντα βαπτισθῆναι* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who hath come to be baptized in the Jordan"); (3) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ὑπὸ Προδρόμου τὸ βάπτισμα αἰτοῦντα [λαβόντα]* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him Who asketh [receiveth] baptism from the Forerunner"); (4) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἐκ τῆς Πατρῴας φωνῆς μαρτυρηθέντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Him to Whom the voice of the Father bore witness"). Three additional bracketed Megalynaria marked with asterisks are preserved from the modern printed Athenian Menaion tradition (ed. Phos, 1960; Apostoliki Diakonia, 1991), although absent from the classical textus receptus of the Violakis Typikon: (5) *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὸν ἕνα τῆς Τριάδος, κλίναντα τὸν αὐχένα, καὶ βάπτισμα λαβόντα* ("Magnify, O my soul, One of the Trinity Who bowed His head and received baptism"); (6) *Προφῆτα, δεῦρο πρός με, ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα, καὶ βάπτισόν με τάχος* ("O Prophet, come unto Me: stretch out thy hand and baptize Me swiftly"); (7) *Προφῆτα, ἄφες ἄρτι, καὶ βάπτισόν με θέλων· πληρῶσαι καὶ γὰρ ἦλθον, πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην* ("O Prophet, suffer it to be so now, and baptize Me willing: for I have come to fulfill all righteousness"). For the Second Iambic Canon, five Megalynaria are provided: (1) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, κλίνει τὸν αὐχένα, χειρὶ τῇ τοῦ Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master bows His head beneath the hand of the Forerunner"); (2) *Σήμερον Ἰωάννης, βαπτίζει τὸν Δεσπότην, ἐν ῥείθροις Ἰορδάνου* ("Today John baptizes the Master in the streams of the Jordan"); and three bracketed Menaion additions: (3) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, νάμασιν ἐνθάπτει, βροτῶν τὴν ἁμαρτίαν* ("Today the Master buries in the waters the sin of mortal man"); (4) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἄνωθεν μαρτυρεῖται, Υἱὸς ἠγαπημένος* ("Today the Master receives testimony from on high, that He is the beloved Son"); (5) *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, ἦλθεν ἁγιάσαι, τὴν φύσιν τῶν ὑδάτων* ("Today the Master has come to sanctify the nature of the waters").
[^222]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of Matins Ode 9, Praises, Great Doxology, and Great Blessing of the Waters Rite (§ 3 concl.). Physical leaf p325 (printed page 310) and facing English leaf p326 (printed page 311) conclude the Ninth Ode and detail the Great Blessing of the Waters celebrated at the climax of the Great Doxology. Ode 9 concludes with the final Megalynaria: *Σήμερον ὁ Δεσπότης, τὸ βάπτισμα λαμβάνει, ὑπὸ χειρὸς Προδρόμου* ("Today the Master receives baptism at the hand of the Forerunner"); "Glory": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τῆς τρισυποστάτου, καὶ ἀδιαιρέτου, θεότητος τὸ κράτος* ("Magnify, O my soul, the power of the Godhead in three Persons and undivided"); "Both now and ever": *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου, τὴν λυτρωσαμένην, ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς κατάρας* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her who hath delivered us from the curse"). Matins continues with the Exapostilarion chanted thrice; at the Praises: 6 Idiomela (*Φῶς ἐκ φωτός* / "Light from Light"); "Glory": *Νάματα Ἰορδάνεια* ("O Savior, Who clothedst Thyself with the waters of Jordan"); "Both now and ever": *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστός* ("Today Christ"), and the Great Doxology. In the Great Doxology, an ancient Constantinopolitan rubrical custom replaces the customary opening verse *Δόξα σοι τῷ δείξαντι τὸ φῶς* ("Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light") with the concluding refrain of the Theotokion: "We who have been enlightened cry aloud: Glory to God made manifest, Who hath appeared upon earth and brought light unto the world." Immediately following the third repetition of the Trisagion (*Ἅγιος ἀθάνατος, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*) at the end of the Doxology, the clergy and choirs transition directly into the solemn Great Blessing of the Waters: the choirs chant the 3 Idiomela of Saint Sophronius of Jerusalem (*Φωνὴ Κυρίου ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων* / "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"), "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ* ("At the voice of one crying in the wilderness"). The Priest exits through the Holy Doors carrying the Precious Cross on his head, preceded by candle-bearers and Deacons; the Patriarch (or presiding Hierarch), vested in epitrachilion and small omophorion, descends from his Throne to the center of the temple where the water vessel has been prepared. The Canonarch reads the three Prophecies (Isaiah 35:1–10; 55:1–13; 12:3–6), followed by the Epistle (1 Corinthians 10:1–4) and the Gospel (Mark 1:9–11) proclaimed by the Patriarch. Following the polychronion (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), the Great Archdeacon intones the Great Litany of the Blessing while the Patriarch recites silently the secret prayer *Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ* ("O Lord Jesus Christ"), culminating in the aloud exclamation *Τριὰς ὑπερούσιε* ("O Trinity transcending essence") and the great festive prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε, καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου* ("Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works"), repeated thrice with the choral acclamation *Δόξα σοι, Κύριε, δόξα σοι!* ("Glory to Thee, O Lord, glory to Thee!"). A critical apparatus note in both Greek and English facsimile columns addresses a numbering error in the 1888 edition, where Violakis misnumbered this footnote as footnote 4 instead of 1; the note documents the pastoral practice emerging in parish churches of delaying the Great Blessing of the Waters until after the Divine Liturgy to prevent disorder and accommodate late-arriving faithful.
[^223]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Continued: Conclusion of the Great Blessing of the Waters and Divine Liturgy Antiphons 1 & 2 (§ 4 opening). Physical leaf p327 (printed page 312) and facing English leaf p328 (printed page 313) conclude the solemn sanctification of waters and commence the festal Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom. Following the thrice-repeated prayer *Μέγας εἶ, Κύριε*, the celebrant immerses the Precious Cross into the water vessel three times with the sprinkler (*ἁγιαστήρ*), chanting each time the Dismissal Troparion of Theophany: *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ βαπτιζομένου σου, Κύριε* ("When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan"), repeated by each choir. He then sprinkles the congregation cruciformly with the newly consecrated water while chanting the Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον τῇ οἰκουμένῃ* ("Thou hast appeared today to the universe"). As the Patriarch ascends the Throne amidst choral acclamations (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*), he sprinkles the concelebrating Hierarchs and clergy; during this sprinkling, the choirs chant slowly and melodiously the Troparion from Ode 8 of the Canon: *Τριάδος ἡ φανέρωσις* ("The manifestation of the Trinity"). The Second Choir then chants the Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom commences immediately. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4), the special festive Antiphons of Theophany are chanted in Tone 2: First Antiphon verses from Psalm 113:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἐν ἐξόδῳ Ἰσραὴλ ἐξ Αἰγύπτου, οἴκου Ἰακώβ* / "When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarian people"; *Ἐγενήθη Ἰουδαία ἁγίασμα αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ ἐξουσία αὐτοῦ* / "Judea became His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion"; *Ἡ θάλασσα εἶδε καὶ ἔφυγεν· ὁ Ἰορδάνης ἐστράφη εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω* / "The sea saw and fled; the Jordan turned back"; *Τί σοί ἐστι θάλασσα, ὅτι ἔφυγες; καὶ σὺ Ἰορδάνη, ὅτι ἐστράφης εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω;* / "What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? And thou, Jordan, that thou didst turn back?"); refrain: *Ταῖς πρεσβείαις τῆς Θεοτόκου, Σῶτερ, σῶσον ἡμᾶς* ("Through the intercessions of the Theotokos, Savior, save us"). Second Antiphon verses from Psalm 114:1, 2, 3, 5 LXX (*Ἠγάπησα, ὅτι εἰσακούσεται Κύριος τῆς φωνῆς τῆς δεήσεώς μου* / "I am well pleased that the Lord will hear the voice of my prayer"; *Ὅτι ἔκλινε τὸ οὖς αὐτοῦ ἐμοί, καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις μου ἐπικαλέσομαι* / "For He hath inclined His ear unto me, and in my days will I call upon Him"; *Περιέσχον με ὠδῖνες θανάτου, κίνδυνοι ᾅδου εὕροσάν με* / "The pangs of death compassed me, the perils of Hades found me; I found tribulation and sorrow"; *Ἐλεήμων ὁ Κύριος καὶ δίκαιος, καὶ ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐλεεῖ* / "Merciful is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful").
[^224]: Feast of Holy Theophany (January 6) Concluded: Divine Liturgy Antiphon 3, Little Entrance, Epistle, Gospel, and Dismissal (§ 4 concl.); and Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (January 7): Friday Vespers (§ 5). Physical leaf p329 (printed page 314) and facing English leaf p330 (printed page 315) conclude the festal Divine Liturgy of Theophany and commence the post-festal Synaxis of the Forerunner celebrated on the following day. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 4 concl.), the Second Antiphon concludes with the refrain *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"), followed by *Ὁ Μονογενὴς Υἱὸς καὶ Λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ* ("Only-begotten Son and Immortal Word of God"). The Third Antiphon is chanted in Tone 1 to verses from Psalm 117:1–4 LXX (*Ἐξομολογεῖσθε τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἀγαθός, ὅτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τὸ ἔλεος αὐτοῦ* / "O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endureth forever"; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἰσραήλ...* / "Let the house of Israel now say..."; *Εἰπάτω δὴ οἶκος Ἀαρών...* / "Let the house of Aaron now say..."; *Εἰπάτωσαν δὴ πάντες οἱ φοβούμενοι τὸν Κύριον...* / "Let all that fear the Lord now say..."); refrain: Dismissal Troparion of Theophany *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*. At the Little Entrance, the festive Introit Verse is chanted from Psalm 117:26, 27 LXX: *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου, Θεὸς Κύριος καὶ ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν. Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου βαπτισθείς, ψάλλοντάς σοι, Ἀλληλούϊα* ("Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God, and hath appeared unto us. Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized by John in the Jordan, who sing to Thee: Alleluia"). Troparia: Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον*. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, the baptismal hymn is chanted: *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε, Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε. Ἀλληλούϊα* ("All of you who have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia", Galatians 3:27). The Epistle of the Feast is Titus 2:11–14; 3:4–7; the Gospel is Matthew 3:13–17. At "Especially", instead of the Axion Estin, the Heirmos of Ode 9 is chanted: *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου τὴν τιμιωτέραν καὶ ἐνδοξοτέραν τῶν ἄνω στρατευμάτων. Ἀπορεῖ πᾶσα γλῶσσα* ("Magnify, O my soul, Her that is more honorable and more glorious than the heavenly hosts. Every tongue is at a loss to praise Thee worthily..."). The Communion Verse is Titus 2:11: *Ἐπεφάνη ἡ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις* ("The grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared unto all men"); instead of *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, Dismissal Troparion *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and the Dismissal. On Friday evening (§ 5), the Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (*Ἡ Σύναξις τοῦ τιμίου Προδρόμου*) is celebrated at Great Vespers: after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 6 Stichira are chanted: 3 Idiomela of the Feast (*Τὸν φωτισμὸν ἡμῶν*) and 3 Prosomoia of the Forerunner (*Πανεύφημε Πρόδρομε Χριστοῦ*); "Glory": *Ἔνσαρκε λύχνε* ("O torch incarnate"); "Both now and ever": *Θεὸς λόγος ἐπεφάνη ἐν σαρκί* ("God the Word appeared in the flesh"). Entrance with *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, followed by the Great Prokeimenon in Tone 7 from Psalm 113:11 LXX: *Ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐν τῇ γῇ, πάντα ὅσα ἠθέλησεν ἐποίησεν* ("Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath willed, He hath done") with its four verses. At the Aposticha: 3 Prosomoia Stichira beginning *Ὡς εἶδέ σε Δέσποτα* ("When he saw Thee, O Master"); "Glory": *Ὡς τοῦ Πνεύματος ἐραστής* ("As a lover of the Spirit"); "Both now and ever": *Δεῦτε μιμησώμεθα* ("Come, let us imitate the wise virgins"); Dismissal Troparia: Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*), and Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου μετ’ ἐγκωμίων* / "The memory of the righteous is celebrated with hymns of praise").
[^225]: Synaxis of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John (January 7) Concluded: Saturday Matins (§ 6), Divine Liturgy (§ 7); and Opening of Sunday after the Lights / Epiphany: Saturday Great Vespers (§ 8). Physical leaf p331 (printed page 316) and facing English leaf p332 (printed page 317) govern the conclusion of the feast of the Synaxis of the Forerunner and the opening of the Sunday after the Lights when January 6 falls on a Friday (Situation 1). Saturday Matins (§ 6) opens following Psalm 50 [LXX] with the Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου μετ’ ἐγκωμίων* / "The memory of the righteous is celebrated with hymns of praise") and the Hexapsalmos. At "God is the Lord" (*Θεὸς Κύριος*), the Dismissal Troparia are chanted as at Vespers: Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*) twice, and Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου*) once; followed by the Psalter Kathisma of Saturday; two Kathismata: *Τοῦ Ἰησοῦ γεννηθέντος* ("When Jesus was born") and *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις βλέψας σε τοῦ Ἰορδάνου* ("When he saw Thee in the streams of the Jordan"), chanted twice each; and Psalm 50 [LXX] read simply. Canons: Canon of the Feast (*Βυθοῦ ἀνεκάλυψε πυθμένα* / "He uncovered the bottom of the deep") with the verse *Δόξα σοι, ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν, δόξα σοι* ("Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee"), and Canon of the Forerunner (*Βαπτιζόμενον* / "Being baptized") with the verse *Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ, πρέσβευε ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν* ("Holy forerunner of God, pray for us"). After Ode 3: Kathismata *Ὁ μέγας ὑετός* ("The great rain") and *Ἑκὼν προῆλθεν ἐπὶ γῆς* ("Willingly He came forth upon earth"). After Ode 6: Kontakion and Ikos of the Forerunner, and the Menologion. The Katavasiai are the Iambic ones only (*Στείβει θαλάσσης* / "The Lord, working wonders"). At Ode 9: First Ode of the festal Ninth Ode with its Megalynaria, and of the Forerunner with the verse *Ἅγιε τοῦ Θεοῦ*, followed by the Katavasia *Μεγάλυνον ψυχή μου... Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν* ("Magnify, O my soul... O the marvels surpassing understanding"). Exapostilaria: of the Forerunner and of the Feast. At the Praises: Idiomela of the Feast as yesterday; "Glory": *Ἄγγελος ἐκ στειρωτικῶν ὠδίνων* ("An angel from barren pangs"); "Both now and ever": *Σήμερον ὁ Χριστὸς ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ* ("Today Christ is in Jordan"); Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion *Μνήμη δικαίου*. At the Divine Liturgy (§ 7): festal Antiphons of Theophany as yesterday; Introit *Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος* ("Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord"); Dismissal Troparia: Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*) and Forerunner (*Μνήμη δικαίου*); a critical apparatus note addresses the omission of the Dismissal Troparion of the Holy Patron of the Temple (omitted here in the 1888 text, but explicitly prescribed in § 39 of the Protheoria and noted in the official Diptycha editions of 1980, 1987, 1990, 1992, and 1993); Kontakion *Ἐπεφάνης σήμερον*. Instead of the Trisagion Hymn, the baptismal hymn *Ὅσοι εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε* ("All of you who have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ", Galatians 3:27) is sung; the Epistle (Acts 19:1–8) and the Gospel (John 1:29–34) of the Forerunner. At "Especially", the Heirmos of Ode 9 *Μεγάλυνον ἡ ψυχή μου... Ὦ τῶν ὑπὲρ νοῦν*. Communion Verse: Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον αἰώνιον ἔσται δίκαιος* / "The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance"); *Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*, and Dismissal. The section for Sunday after the Lights / Epiphany opens at § 8: on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and Kathisma 1 of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried" (*Κύριε ἐκέκραξα*), 10 Stichira are sung: 6 Resurrectional and 4 of the Afterfeast in appointed sequence; "Glory": *Κύριε πληρῶσαι βουλόμενος* ("O Lord, wishing to fulfill...", seek at the Glory of the Lite); "Both now and ever": first Theotokion of the Tone; Entrance with *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon *Ὁ Κύριος ἐβασίλευσεν* (Ps. 92:1 LXX). At the Aposticha, the Resurrectional Stichira are sung.

Both now and ever...": *Σήμερον ἡ κτίσις φωτίζεται* ("Today creation is illumined", seek in the Lite); Dismissal Troparia: Resurrectional, and Theophany (*Ἐν Ἰορδάνῃ*), and Dismissal. At "Especially", *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Verse: Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* / "Praise the Lord from the heavens"); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν*, and Dismissal. At § 11, the Apodosis of the Feast in Situation 1 (Theophany on Friday) falls on the Saturday of the following week (January 14): the entire festal office of Theophany is repeated, omitting the Old Testament Readings at Vespers, and the Lite, Polyeleos, and festal Gospel at Matins; at the Divine Liturgy, the Epistle (Colossians 1:3–6) and Gospel (Luke 16:10–15) of the Saturday after the Lights are appointed. Leaf p333 concludes with the heading for Situation Two (*Β΄*), governing the calendar when Holy Theophany occurs on a Saturday.
[^227]: Situation 2 (Theophany on Saturday): Friday Royal Hours, Vespers, Liturgy of St. Basil (§ 12); Saturday Theophany Matins, Great Blessing of Waters, Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom (§ 13); Sunday after the Lights & Synaxis of the Forerunner: Saturday Great Vespers (§ 14) and Sunday Matins through Ode 9 (§ 15 opening). Critical Apparatus Note 2 preserves Violakis's rubrical rule for the lectionary when January 14 coincides with the opening of the Lenten Triodion (Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee): under standard conditions, the Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday after the Lights (Ephesians 4:7–13; Matthew 4:12–17) are transferred to the following Sunday (January 14), which is the Apodosis of Theophany. If, however, January 14 is the Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee, the Triodion lections cannot be superseded; therefore, on January 7, the Epistle of the Forerunner is read alongside the Gospel of the Sunday after the Lights. The rubric transitions at centered heading *Γ΄* to Situation Three, when Holy Theophany falls on a Sunday. At § 20: on Friday morning (January 4), following daily Matins, only the Great Royal Hours are celebrated, with Troparion *Ἑτοιμάζου Ζαβουλών* ("Make ready, O Zebulun") and Kontakion *Ἐν τοῖς ῥείθροις σήμερον* ("Today the Lord hath appeared in the streams of the Jordan"); after the Prayer of the Ninth Hour, the Dismissal. At table, dispensation for all foods (*κατάλυσις εἰς πάντα*) is observed, without fasting, because the Paramony strict fast is transferred to Saturday. At § 21: on Friday evening, Forefeast Vespers is sung according to the Menaion; after *Νῦν ἀπολύεις* ("Lord, now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", Luke 2:29–32), the Canon is sung, and after the Heirmos of Ode 9, the Trisagion Prayers, the Dismissal Troparion *Ἀπεστρέφετό ποτε* ("The river Jordan once turned back"), and Dismissal. At § 22: Saturday Matins opens following the Midnight Service, with the reading of the Psalter Kathismata, followed by the Canons of the Forefeast and of the Saints.

Scholarly Rubrical Table "Notes Concerning the Epistle and Gospel Readings" (Σημειώσεις περὶ Ἀποστόλου καὶ Εὐαγγελίου) resolving the movable Lucan and Matthaean leaps: Case 1: If one Sunday intervenes between Sunday after the Lights and the First Sunday of the Triodion: Epistle of 32nd Sunday (1 Timothy 4:9–15) and Gospel of Zacchaeus (15th Sunday of Luke, Luke 19:1–10). Case 2: If two Sundays intervene: First Sunday: Epistle 29th (Colossians 3:4–11), Gospel of Ten Lepers (12th Sunday of Luke, Luke 17:12–19); Second Sunday: Epistle 32nd, Gospel of Zacchaeus. Case 3: If three Sundays intervene: First Sunday: Epistle 29th, Gospel of Ten Lepers; Second Sunday: Epistle 32nd, Gospel of Zacchaeus; Third Sunday: Epistle 17th (2 Corinthians 6:16–7:1), Gospel of Canaanite Woman (17th Sunday of Matthew, Matthew 15:21–28). Case 4: If four Sundays intervene: First Sunday: Epistle 29th, Gospel of Ten Lepers; Second Sunday: Epistle 31st (1 Timothy 1:15–17), Gospel 13th of Luke (The Rich Ruler, Luke 18:18–27); Third Sunday: Epistle 32nd, Gospel of Zacchaeus; Fourth Sunday: Epistle 17th, Gospel of Canaanite Woman. Rubrical Note on Late Paschal Calculations (incipit): When Pascha is late and daily Liturgies lack Gospels after the Lucan cycle is completed before the Triodion begins, the remaining Matthaean weeks prior to the Elevation of the Holy Cross are counted and read; likewise for Epistles. Textual and Hymnographical Note: The Heirmos of the Eighth Ode of the First Canon to Saint Euthymius, composed by Saint John of Damascus, appears in later printed editions as *Παῖδας εὐαγεῖς ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ* ("The holy Children in the furnace"); however, the alphabetical acrostic *Ὄλβος πέφηνας γηγενῶν Εὐθύμιε* ("A wealth to mortals hast thou appeared, O Euthymius") demands that the Eighth Ode begin with the letter *Y* (Upsilon). In the Venice 1533 Menaion of Stephanos Savios, the Heirmos begins *Υἱοὺς τῆς Σιὼν ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ* ("Sons of Zion in the furnace"), preserving the ancient and genuine poetic reading per the judgment of Patriarch Constantius I. Scholarly Rubrical Decree of Patriarch Constantine I the Byzantine concerning the Praises on Sundays: Explains the standard rubrical canon prescribing the Resurrectional Eothinon Doxastikon at "Glory..." at the Praises on ordinary Sundays of the year, but establishes that for the great Ecumenical Doctors Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom, out of just debt to their pastoral guidance and immortal writings illuminating the Catholic Church, when their commemorations coincide with a Sunday outside the Triodion, the Doxastikon of the Saint is chanted instead of the Eothinon, especially in the Great Church of Constantinople. Note on Footnote 3: When this commemoration occurs on a Sunday within the Triodion period, the Doxastikon of the Triodion is chanted at "Glory..." at the Praises. Physical leaf p365 (printed page 350) and facing English leaf p366 (printed page 351) record the patriarchal decrees governing the precedence of Doxastika at the Praises for the Great Hierarchs.

[^250]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord, God and Savior Jesus Christ (Hypapante, February 2) — Case I: Weekday Celebration (Conclusion of Matins: Ode 9 Megalynaria): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p381 (printed page 366) and facing English leaf p382 (printed page 367). Following the initial Megalynarion *Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι* (inaugurated on leaf p380), the ninth ode of the Canon of the Meeting (composed by Saint Cosmas of Maiuma and embellished by the Byzantine sticheraric tradition) presents an alphabetical series of ten nine-syllable/twelve-syllable Megalynaria addressed alternately to the Theotokos, Christ, and the Righteous Symeon: (1) concluding verse of initial incipit: *Ἀγγέλοις καὶ βροτοῖς, Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή* ["...unto angels and mortal men, O pure Virgin Mother"]; (2) *Ἀγκαλίζεται χερσίν, ὁ Πρεσβύτης Συμεών* ["Symeon the Elder takes in his arms the Maker of the Law and Master of all"]; (3) *Βουληθεὶς ὁ Πλαστουργός, ἵνα σώσῃ τὸν Ἀδάμ* ["The Creator, wishing to save Adam, took up His dwelling in thy pure and virgin womb"]; (4) *Γένος ἅπαν τῶν βροτῶν, μακαρίζει σε Ἁγνή* ["All the race of mortals blesseth thee, O Pure Virgin, and in faith glorifieth thee as Mother of God"]; (5) *Δεῦτε ἴδετε Χριστόν, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Come and behold Christ, the Master of all, Whom Symeon beareth today in the temple"]; (6) *Ἐπιβλέπεις πρὸς τὴν γῆν, καὶ ποιεῖς τρέμειν αὐτήν* ["Thou lookest upon the earth and makest it tremble; how then can I, aged and weary, hold Thee in mine arms?"]; (7) *Ζήσας ἔτη Συμεών, ἕως εἶδε τὸν Χριστόν* ["Symeon lived for many years until he beheld Christ, and cried aloud unto Him: 'Now do I seek release'"]; (8) *Ἡ λαβὶς ἡ μυστική, ἡ τὸν ἄνθρακα Χριστόν* ["Thou art the mystic tongs, Mary, who hast conceived in thy womb Christ the live Coal" — drawing upon Isaiah 6:6]; (9) *Θέλων ἐνηνθρώπησας, ὁ προάναρχος Θεός* ["Of Thine own will Thou didst become man, O God without beginning, and art brought into the temple, forty days of age"]; (10) *Κατελθόντ’ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, τὸν Δεσπότην τοῦ παντός* ["Symeon the priest received the Master of all, Who came down from heaven"]. Rubrical expansion of the 4 Troparia of Ode 9 to 6 with their proper appointed Megalynaria: Troparion 1 *Ἐν νόμῳ σκιᾷ* with Megalynarion *Λάμπρυνόν μου τὴν ψυχήν*; Troparion 2 with Megalynarion *Μητροπάρθενε ἁγνή, τί προσφέρεις*; Troparion 3 *Τοῖς πρὶν νεογνῶν* with Megalynarion *Νῦν ἀπόλυσιν ζητῶ*; Troparion 4 with Megalynarion *Ὃν οἱ ἄνω λειτουργοί*; Doxastikon (*Δόξα*) with Triadikon *Ἡ τῇ φύσει μὲν μονάς* ["O Thou Who art by nature One, but in Persons Three..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἀπέδωκάς μοι*; and Theotokion (*Καὶ νῦν*) *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς* ["O Theotokos, Hope of all Christians, shelter, guard, and preserve those whose hope is in thee..."] paired with Megalynarion *Ἱεροπρεπῶς ἀνθωμολογεῖτο*.

Scholarly Note 1: Editorial note regarding the calendrical impossibility of the Apodosis of the Meeting occurring on a Sunday outside the Triodion period (under the Julian/Paschal calendar, Pascha falls between March 22 and April 25; the Triodion begins between January 11 and February 15; if February 9 falls on a Sunday, it is invariably within the Triodion, either as Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee, Prodigal Son, or Meatfare). § 11 incipit: Situation II: Concurrence when February 2 falls on a Sunday within the Triodion period: Saturday Great Vespers (at "Lord, I have cried": 4 Resurrectional Stichira, 2 of Triodion, and 4 of Feast [on Meatfare and Cheesefare Sundays: 4 Resurrectional, 3 of Triodion, 3 of Feast]; "Glory...": of Triodion; "Both now and ever...": of Feast; Little Entrance, Prokeimenon, Old Testament Readings; Aposticha: Resurrectional Stichira, "Glory...": of Triodion, "Both now and ever...": of Feast...).
[^255]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ (Hypapante, February 2) — Situation II Conclusion (§§ 12–13) and Sunday After the Feast Within the Triodion (§ 12 concl.): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p391 (printed page 376) and facing English leaf p392 (printed page 377). Paragraph 12 completes the rubrical order for Sunday Matins when February 2 falls on a Sunday within the pre-Lenten Triodion period (Publican and Pharisee, Prodigal Son, Meatfare, or Cheesefare). Following the Triadic Canon and festal Litiya (with Triodion Doxastikon when appointed), the Hexapsalmos and "God is the Lord" (*Θεὸς Κύριος*) lead into the distribution of Kathismata across three Stichologiai: Resurrectional Kathismata combined with festal Kathismata *Χορὸς Ἀγγελικός* and *Ὁ ὢν σὺν τῷ Πατρί*, while the third festal Kathisma *Νηπιάζει δι’ ἐμέ* is sung twice. After the Hypakoe and Anavathmoi of the Tone, the Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX) and festal Liturgy Gospel are proclaimed. The Canons of the Resurrection, Triodion, and Feast are chanted; after Ode 3, the Resurrectional Kontakion/Ikos and Kathismata; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos, festal Menologion, and Triodion Synaxarion [Hypomnema]. Ode 9 features festal Megalynaria (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) with Troparia and Katavasia *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς. . . Ἐν νόμῳ, σκιᾷ*. Praises combine 4 Resurrectional and 4 festal Stichira (modified to 3 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 Feast on Meatfare and Cheesefare Sundays). Paragraph 13 establishes the Divine Liturgy order: festal Antiphons from Psalm 44 LXX with the Christological refrain *Σῶσον ἡμᾶς, Υἱὲ Θεοῦ, ὁ ἐν ἀγκάλαις τοῦ Δικαίου Συμεὼν βασταχθείς...* and Sunday Little Entrance Introit Psalm 97:2 LXX (*Ἐγνώρισε Κύριος* with *ὁ ἀναστὰς ἐκ νεκρῶν*); Dismissal Troparion *Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*, Kontakion *Ὁ μήτραν παρθενικήν*, festal Epistle and Sunday Gospel, Ode 9 Megalynarion, Communion Verse Psalm 115:4 LXX, and the composite festal-resurrectional Dismissal.
