Paragraph 17 completes Sunday Matins for the festal Apodosis within the Triodion: after Psalm 50 LXX, Triadic Canon, and Triodion Litiya Idiomelon (if present), Kathismata across three Stichologiai (Resurrectional paired with festal); Canons of Resurrection, Triodion, and Feast; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion, Triodion and festal Kathismata; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos and Menologion; Katavasiai *Χέρσον ἀβυσσοτόκον*, festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) with Troparia and Katavasia *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς. . . Ἐν νόμῳ, σκιᾷ*; Praises with 4 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 festal Stichira; "Glory...": Triodion, "Both now and ever...": Feast (*Ὁ ἐν χερσὶ πρεσβυτικαῖς*). Paragraph 18 governs the Divine Liturgy: festal Antiphons from Psalm 44 LXX, Entrance Hymn Psalm 97:2 LXX with Sunday refrain, festal and Sunday Troparia/Kontakion, Sunday Epistle and Gospel, Ode 9 Megalynarion, and Communion Verse Psalm 115:4 LXX. Paragraph 19 resolves Situation III: when the Feast of the Meeting coincides with Meatfare Saturday (the Saturday of Souls): the ancestral rubrics of the ancient Typika and the authoritative rulings of Patriarchs Constantios I (1830–1834) and Gregory VI (1835–1840, 1867–1871) mandate that the entire Office of the Souls be transferred to the preceding Saturday (the Saturday before the Sunday of the Prodigal Son), so that the Feast of the Meeting may be celebrated on its own day without displacement or abbreviation according to the primary rubrics of §§ 1–3.
[^258]: Variable Calendrical Cases for the Apodosis of the Meeting (Cases 1–5) and Cheesefare Sunday Evening Vespers (§ 20 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p397 (printed page 382) and facing English leaf p398 (printed page 383). The Typikon provides a rigorous 5-case combinatorial matrix for fixing the date of the Apodosis of the Meeting based upon its interaction with the movable pre-Lenten Triodion cycle: Case 1 [α΄]: Feast occurs between Sunday of Publican and Pharisee and Friday of that week -> Apodosis on regular 8th day (February 9); Case 2 [β΄]: Feast occurs between Saturday eve of Prodigal Son and Tuesday of Meatfare Week -> Apodosis celebrated early on Friday before the Saturday of Souls, because the ancestral Office of the Dead on Meatfare Saturday is inviolable and cannot be displaced for an Apodosis; Case 3 [γ΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday of Meatfare Week and Saturday of Souls -> Apodosis postponed to Tuesday of Cheesefare Week; Case 4 [δ΄]: Feast occurs between Meatfare Sunday and Tuesday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis on Friday of Cheesefare Week; Case 5 [ε΄]: Feast occurs between Wednesday and Saturday of Cheesefare Week -> Apodosis celebrated on Cheesefare Sunday per §§ 16–18. When the Feast itself falls on Cheesefare Sunday (celebrated per §§ 11–13), the Apodosis is celebrated that same evening at Forgiveness Vespers (§ 20): "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Stichira of the Feast and 3 of the Righteous Symeon; Great Prokeimenon *Μὴ ἀποστρέψῃς* (Psalm 68:18 LXX); Aposticha Idiomelon *Ἔλαμψεν ἡ χάρις σου* and festal Theotokion; proper festal Dismissal followed immediately by the Forgiveness rite without the customary priestly blessing *Δι’ εὐχῶν*.
[^259]: Cheesefare Sunday Evening Forgiveness Vespers Conclusion (§ 20 concl.) and Situation IV: Clean Monday Concurrence (§§ 21–22): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p399 (printed page 384) and facing English leaf p400 (printed page 385). Paragraph 20 concludes the Forgiveness Vespers rite marking the opening of Great Lent: following the festal Dismissal of the Meeting (omitting *Δι’ εὐχῶν*), the Choirs chant the penitential Troparion *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε*, 40 *Κύριε ἐλέησον*, *Ὁ ὢν εὐλογητός*, the Prayer of Saint Ephrem with Great Prostrations [Metanias], the Deacon/Priest litany *Εὐξώμεθα ὑπὲρ εἰρήνης τοῦ κόσμου*, and the hymn *Πάντων προστατεύεις* while clergy and faithful exchange the kiss of peace and mutual forgiveness, formally concluding the Apodosis of the Feast. Paragraphs 21–22 formulate Situation IV: when February 2 coincides with Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): on Cheesefare Sunday evening at Vespers (§ 21), "Lord, I have cried" combines 3 Triodion fasting Idiomela (*Ἐγκρατείᾳ τὴν σάρκα*) and 3 festal Stichira (*Λέγε Συμεών*), Great Prokeimenon Psalm 133:1 LXX (*Ἰδοὺ δὴ εὐλογεῖτε τὸν Κύριον*), Old Testament Readings of the Feast, and festal Aposticha; on Clean Monday at Matins (§ 22), the festal Litiya and "God is the Lord" lead into Kathismata across three Stichologiai combining Triodion fasting hymns (*Τῆς νηστείας τῇ θείᾳ ἀπαρχῇ*, *Τὴν πάνσεπτον ἐγκράτειαν*) with festal Kathismata; Anavathmoi (Antiphon 1 of Tone 4), Prokeimenon (Psalm 44:18 LXX), and festal Morning Gospel; Canon to 6 with festal Megalynaria of Ode 9 (*Ἀκατάληπτόν ἐστι*) and festal Exapostilarion *Ἐν πνεύματι τῷ Ἱερῷ* thrice; Praises combining festal Stichira Prosomia *Νόμον τὸν ἐν γράμματι* and festal Doxastikon *Ὁ ἐν χερσὶ πρεσβυτικαῖς*, concluding with the Great Doxology.
[^260]: Feast of the Meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ (February 2) — Clean Monday Liturgy Conclusion (§ 23), Apodosis of the Meeting (§ 24), and February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos (Heading & Situation I, § 1): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p401 (printed page 386) and facing English leaf p402 (printed page 387). Paragraph 23 completes the rubrical order for the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom when the Meeting coincides with Clean Monday (the first day of Great Lent): festal Antiphons from Psalm 44 LXX, Entrance Hymn Psalm 97:2 LXX, Dismissal Troparion *Χαῖρε κεχαριτωμένη*, Kontakion *Ὁ μήτραν παρθενικήν*, festal Epistle and Gospel, Ode 9 Megalynarion *Θεοτόκε ἡ ἐλπίς . . . Ἐν νόμῳ σκιᾷ*, Communion Verse Psalm 115:4 LXX (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου*), and proper festal Dismissal with Christological incipit *Ὁ ἐν ἀγκάλαις τοῦ Δικαίου Συμεὼν βασταχθῆναι καταδεξάμενος διὰ τὴν ἡμῶν σωτηρίαν...*; the dispensation permitting wine and oil on Clean Monday is explicitly confirmed. Paragraph 24 establishes the Apodosis of the Meeting on Clean Monday evening: Vespers is chanted without variation per § 1, omitting Old Testament Readings; Dismissal Troparion thrice, Dismissal, and formal Apodosis; Great Compline is omitted out of festal reverence, replaced by Small Compline recited in cells in city churches, while monasteries observe their founder Typika (per Patriarchs Constantios I and Gregory VI). The general occurrence rule notes the Meeting may fall between the Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee and Clean Monday per the 34 Paschalia table. Commemoration of February 10 (Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos) begins with Situation I (§ 1): occurrence on any weekday from the beginning of the Triodion through Cheesefare Friday is governed entirely by the Menaion; Matins Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; Liturgy Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*.
[^261]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation II: Concurrence on Sunday Outside the Triodion (§ 2) and Situation III: Concurrence on First Four Sundays of the Triodion (§§ 3–4, § 5 incipit): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p403 (printed page 388) and facing English leaf p404 (printed page 389). Paragraph 2 governs Situation II when February 10 falls on a Sunday outside the Triodion cycle: the Saint's Office is combined with the Resurrectional Office as customary for ranked feasts on Sundays; Praises Doxastikon is the Eothinon Gospel Sticheron; Epistle of the Saint, Gospel of the Sunday; Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*; Communion Verse Psalm 148:1 LXX (*Αἰνεῖτε*). Paragraphs 3–5 govern Situation III when the feast occurs on one of the first four Sundays of the Triodion (Publican and Pharisee, Prodigal Son, Meatfare, or Cheesefare): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers (§ 3), 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine 4 Resurrectional, 3 Triodion, and 3 of the Saint; Doxastikon of the Triodion, first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; Old Testament Readings of the Saint; Aposticha Resurrectional with Doxastikon of the Saint and Theotokion of the Triodion; Dismissal Troparia of Resurrection, Saint, and Theotokion. On Sunday at Matins (§ 4): after Psalm 50 LXX, Triadic Canon, festal Litiya of the Saint, Hexapsalmos, and "God is the Lord"; Psalter and Polyeleos; Resurrectional Kathismata with 3rd Kathisma of the Saint; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, Prokeimenon; Canons of Resurrection, Triodion, and Saint; after Ode 3, Resurrectional Kontakion/Ikos and Kathismata of the Saint, Triodion, and Theotokion; after Ode 6, Triodion Kontakion/Ikos, Menologion of the Saint, and Sunday Synaxarion; Triodion Katavasiai; Eothinon Gospel sequence; *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*; Exapostilaria of Resurrection, Triodion, Saint, and Theotokion; Praises with 3 Resurrectional, 2 Triodion, and 3 Saint Stichira; Triodion Doxastikon, *Ὑπερευλογημένη*, Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Paragraph 5 begins the Divine Liturgy order with Typika and Beatitudes (4 of Tone, 4 of Ode 6 of Triodion Canon).

Paragraph 8 opens the Divine Liturgy with festal Antiphons and Entrance Hymn Psalm 97:2 LXX (*Ἐγνώρισε Κύριος*).

Paragraph 23 establishes the order for Great Vespers on Saturday evening: after Introductory Psalm 103 LXX and Psalter (Kathisma 1), at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine 4 Resurrectional, 3 Triodion, and 3 Prosomia of the Saint; Doxastikon of the Triodion, first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; Little Entrance, "O Gladsome Light", Prokeimenon, and Old Testament Readings of the Saint; Aposticha Resurrectional with Doxastikon of the Saint and Theotokion of the Triodion; Dismissal Troparia of the Resurrection, the Triodion (*Τὴν ἄχραντον εἰκόνα σου*, "Thy pure icon do we venerate", Tone 2), the Saint, the Theotokion, and Dismissal. [^269]: February 10: Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos — Situation XIV: Monday & Tuesday of Second Week of Lent (§§ 26–28); Triodion Feasibility Envelope; and February 24 Heading: Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p419 (printed page 404) and facing English leaf p420 (printed page 405). Paragraph 28 governs Tuesday of the Second Week per §§ 13–15. The concluding rubrical note outlines the occurrence envelope of St. Charalampos: falling between the Sunday of the Publican and Pharisee and Tuesday of the Second Week of Great Lent per the Heortodromion table. The monument then introduces the feast of February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Honorable Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (*Ἡ α΄ καὶ β΄ εὕρεσις τῆς τιμίας κεφαλῆς τοῦ Προδρόμου*).
[^270]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situations I through V (§§ 1–5): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p421 (printed page 406) and facing English leaf p422 (printed page 407). Paragraph 1 establishes Situation I: when February 24 falls on any weekday (Monday through Saturday) between Thursday of the Week of the Prodigal Son and Friday of Cheesefare Week, the service is chanted entirely as set forth in the Menaion. Paragraph 2 governs Situation II: when the feast concurs with the Saturday of Souls (Meatfare Saturday, the universal commemoration of all deceased Orthodox Christians), the service of the Forerunner is transferred and chanted in advance on Friday alongside the commemoration of the Holy Hieromartyr Polycarp of Smyrna (February 23), whereas the Saturday of Souls remains immoveable on Saturday. Paragraph 3 governs Situation III: when the feast falls on Meatfare Sunday or Cheesefare Sunday, the order of service conforms exactly to the typikon rubrics governing the commemoration of the Holy Hieromartyr Charalampos (February 10) under Situation Three, Paragraphs 3, 4, and 5 (combining Resurrectional hymns, Triodion propers, and feast hymns). Paragraph 4 governs Situation IV: when the feast falls on Cheesefare Saturday (the commemoration of all the Holy Ascetic Fathers and Mothers), the service follows the order of St. Charalampos under Situation Six, Paragraphs 10 and 11. Paragraph 5 governs Situation V: when February 24 falls on Clean Monday (the first day of the Great Fast), the service of the Forerunner cannot be celebrated on a strict Lenten aliturgical day and is chanted in advance on Cheesefare Sunday according to the order of St. Charalampos under Situation Three, Paragraphs 3, 4, and 5.
[^271]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situation VI: Concurrence on Tuesday of the First Week of Great Lent (§§ 6–8): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p423 (printed page 408) and facing English leaf p424 (printed page 409). Paragraph 6 details the service of Vespers celebrated on Clean Monday morning: after Introductory Psalm 103 LXX, at "Lord, I have cried", 6 Stichira combine 3 cycle Prosomia from the Triodion and 3 of the Forerunner (*Χαίροις ἡ ἱερὰ κεφαλή*, "Rejoice, O sacred head"); Doxastikon and Prosomion Theotokion; "O Gladsome Light", Old Testament Readings of the Triodion; at the Aposticha, the Triodion Idiomelon is chanted twice and the Martyrikon once, followed by "Glory... Both now and ever...", Theotokion, "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" (Luke 2:29), Trisagion Prayers, the kneeling troparion *Θεοτόκε Παρθένε* ("O Virgin Theotokos"), and Dismissal. Paragraph 7 details Tuesday Matins and the Hours: after the Hexapsalmos, at "God is the Lord", the Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner *Ἐκ γῆς ἀνατείλασα* ("Having arisen from the earth", Tone 4) is chanted twice, followed by the Theotokion; Psalter and Kathismata in order; Anavathmoi (Tone 4, First Antiphon); Prokeimenon Psalm 131:17 LXX (*Ἐκεῖ ἐξανατελῶ κέρας τῷ Δαβίδ*); "Let every breath praise the Lord" and the Morning Gospel (Luke 7:17–30); Psalm 50 LXX read plainly, *Ταῖς τοῦ σοῦ Προδρόμου* ("Through the intercessions of Thy Forerunner"), *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*, Psalm 50:3 LXX, and the Idiomelon *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν* ("The divine treasure"); Canons: the Theotokos Canon *Ὑγρὰν διοδεύσας* and the Canon of the Forerunner; Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*; after "More honorable than the Cherubim", the Exapostilarion of the Forerunner and Theotokion; at the Praises, 4 Prosomia *Ἤνοιξε Προπύλαια* ("He opened the fore-doors"), Doxastikon *Τὴν πανσεβάσμιον κάραν* ("The all-venerable head"), Theotokion *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος* ("O Theotokos, thou art the true vine"), Great Doxology, and Dismissal Troparion; plain Hours are read with the Troparion and Kontakion *Προφῆτα Θεοῦ καὶ Πρόδρομε* ("O Prophet of God and Forerunner"); at the Ninth Hour, the Beatitudes and penitential troparia are chanted per St. Charalampos Situation Eight, Paragraph 14. Paragraph 8 details the Divine Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts celebrated on Tuesday: at Vespers, Kathisma 18 (Psalms 119–133 LXX), 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" (Triodion Aposticha Idiomelon twice, Martyrikon, 3 Triodion Prosomia, 4 Forerunner *Δεῦτε τὴν τιμίαν κεφαλήν*, "Come, let us honor the precious head"), Doxastikon *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν*, Stavrotheotokion; Little Entrance with the Gospel Book, "O Gladsome Light", Triodion Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω* (Psalm 140:2 LXX), Epistle 2 Corinthians 4:6–15, Gospel Matthew 11:2–15, *Νῦν αἱ δυνάμεις*, Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX (*Εἰς μνημόσυνον*), Psalm 33:2 LXX, and Dismissal.

Paragraph 9 governs Situation VII: when February 24 falls on Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday of the First Week of Great Lent, the typikon order follows the model of St. Charalampos under Situations Nine and Eleven, Paragraphs 16 and 18 (the printed Greek text exhibits a numerical reference citation to §§ 12 and 16, which corresponds structurally to the respective Wednesday and Friday rubrics of the St. Charalampos section). Paragraph 10 governs Situation VIII: when the feast falls on Saturday of the First Week of Great Lent (Theodore Saturday, commemorating the Miracle of the Kolyva wrought by the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit): on Friday morning at Vespers, 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine the day's Idiomelon *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ ἐπεργασώμεθα* ("Come, ye faithful, let us work", twice), 4 Prosomia of the Forerunner, and 4 of St. Theodore; Doxastikon of St. Theodore *Ὀργάνῳ χρησάμενος* ("Using the apostate emperor as his tool"), and the first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone occurring; Little Entrance with the censer, "O Gladsome Light", Old Testament Readings of the Triodion, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, *Νῦν αἱ δυνάμεις*, Communion Verse Psalm 33:9 LXX (*Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε*, "O taste and see"), Psalm 33:2 LXX, and Dismissal. [^273]: February 24: First and Second Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner — Situation IX and Situation X Opening (§§ 12–14): Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p427 (printed page 412) and facing English leaf p428 (printed page 413). Paragraph 12 governs Situation IX: when February 24 concurs with the First Sunday of Great Lent (Sunday of Orthodoxy), the order follows the rubrics for St. Charalampos under Situation Thirteen, Paragraphs 23–25. Footnote 2 of the Greek source text notes an important historical witness: the Typikon of the Great Church compiled under Emperor Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus (*Τὸ τοῦ Κωνσταντίνου Τυπικὸν*) transfers the feast of the Forerunner to the Saturday of the Second Week of Great Lent (falling on March 1 or 2 in that calendar configuration) to prevent overshadowing the Sunday of Orthodoxy. Paragraph 13 establishes Situation X: when February 24 falls on the Second Sunday of Great Lent (commemoration of St. Gregory Palamas, Archbishop of Thessalonica): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, after Introductory Psalm 103 LXX and Kathisma 1 of the Psalter, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine 4 Resurrectional of the Tone, 3 of the Forerunner, and 3 of St. Gregory; Doxastikon of the Triodion, and first Dogmatic Theotokion of the Tone; Little Entrance, "O Gladsome Light", and Saturday evening Prokeimenon; at the Aposticha, the Resurrectional Stichira, Doxastikon of the Forerunner *Ἡ τῶν θείων ἐννοιῶν*, Theotokion *Ὢ θαύματος καινοῦ* ("O strange marvel"), and Dismissal Troparia of the Resurrection, the Forerunner, St. Gregory, and Theotokion. Paragraph 17 provides the general rule for Monday occurrences during the Second, Third, or Fourth Weeks of Great Lent, directing the celebrant to St. Charalampos Situation Fourteen, Paragraphs 26 and 27, and indicating that all remaining unstated weekday occurrences likewise resolve according to the general rubrics established for St. Charalampos. The concluding rubric summarizes the liturgical occurrence envelope: according to the Paschal calculation table (Heortodromion), February 24 can fall within the Triodion season between Thursday of the Week of the Prodigal Son and Tuesday of the Fourth Week of Great Lent.

Paragraph 6 establishes Situation III: when the feast falls on Friday of the First Week, on Thursday morning Vespers is chanted as in Situation I, Paragraph 1, and on Friday morning Matins and the Hours follow Situation I, Paragraph 2; at Friday Vespers, after Kathisma 18, 10 Stichira at "Lord, I have cried" combine the Idiomelon *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ* twice, 4 Prosomia of the Martyrs, and 4 of the Great Martyr Theodore the Recruit; Doxastikon *Ἐν ᾠδαῖς ἀσμάτων*, first Theotokion of the Tone occurring, Little Entrance with the Holy Gospel Book, "O Gladsome Light", Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, Epistle and Gospel of the Martyrs, Presanctified Liturgy with Communion Verse Psalm 111:6 LXX, and Dismissal. On Friday evening, the Ikoi of the Akathist Hymn (First Stasis) are read with Kontakion *Πίστιν Χριστοῦ* ("Thy faith in Christ was like a breastplate"). The rubric notes that on Friday of the Second, Third, and Fourth Weeks the same order is kept, omitting the Stichira of St. Theodore and chanting the day's Idiomelon twice, 4 Martyrika, and 4 of the Martyrs. Paragraph 7 establishes Situation IV: when the feast falls on Saturday of the First Week (Theodore Saturday, commemorating the Miracle of the Kolyva): on Friday morning at Vespers, after Kathisma 18, 10 Stichira combine *Δεῦτε πιστοὶ* twice, 4 of the Martyrs, and 4 of St. Theodore; Doxastikon of St. Theodore *Ὀργάνῳ χρησάμενος*, first Theotokion of the Tone, Little Entrance with the censer, "O Gladsome Light", Readings, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, Presanctified Liturgy with Communion Verse Psalm 33:9 LXX (*Γεύσασθε καὶ ἴδετε*), and Dismissal.

[^284]: March 9: Commemoration of the Holy Forty Martyrs of Sebastea — Situation XII Conclusion (§ 21, Festal Range Note); March 25: The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos — Paramony Rubric and Situation I Opening (§ 1). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p449 (printed page 434) and facing English leaf p450 (printed page 435). Paragraph 21 concludes Situation XII: at the Divine Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom, Typika and Beatitudes appoint 4 troparia from Ode 3 of the Theotokos and 4 from Ode 6 of the Saints; at the Little Entrance, the Third Antiphon refrain is chanted: "O come, let us worship and bow down before Christ; save us, O Son of God, wondrous art Thou in the Saints, who sing to Thee: Alleluia", followed by Troparion *Τὸ προσταχθὲν μυστικῶς*, that of the Saints, the Temple Patron, and Kontakion *Τῇ ὑπερμάχῳ*; Epistle of the Saints and Gospel *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* (Luke 1:39–49, 56); Megalynarion at "Especially": *Ἅπας γηγενής*; Communion Verse: Psalm 115:4 LXX (*Ποτήριον σωτηρίου*); *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. The general rubric notes that the Feast of the Forty Martyrs can fall within the Triodion cycle between Wednesday of the First Week of Great Lent and Great and Holy Monday of Passion Week. For March 25 (The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos), the Paramony Rubric distinguishes cathedral/parish usage from monastic typika: when the Eve falls on Wednesday or Friday, parish churches do not celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy because they do not hold an all-night vigil (except on Great and Holy Tuesday and Wednesday), whereas monasteries celebrate the Presanctified Liturgy combined with Small Vespers according to ancient founder typika. Paragraph 1 establishes Situation I: when the Annunciation falls on Friday of the 3rd Week of Great Lent, on Wednesday morning at Vespers of the Presanctified, after Kathisma 18, at "Lord, I have cried", 10 Stichira combine the day's Idiomelon twice, Martyrikon once, 3 Prosomia of the sequence of the Triodion, and 4 Forefeast Prosomia *Κεκρυμμένον μυστήριον*; Doxastikon *Εὐαγγελίζεται ὁ Γαβριὴλ*, Little Entrance with "O Gladsome Light", Readings of the day, *Κατευθυνθήτω*, and the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts follows in due order.

The Historical Note documents that in 1881, under Ecumenical Patriarch Joachim III, when the Annunciation fell on Wednesday of the 5th Week, a Synodical decree appointed the Great Canon to be chanted at Small Compline on Wednesday evening immediately following the Apodosis Vespers, followed on Thursday morning by Matins and Presanctified Liturgy.

Paragraph 69 introduces Situation XXIII: concurrence on Holy and Great Friday or Holy and Great Saturday: the Feast is transferred and celebrated on Easter Sunday itself together with the Resurrection Office. Violakis transcribes the canonical decree of the Ecumenical Patriarchate: "The Holy and Great Church of Christ, having received this tradition from Patriarchs and Hierarchs from a century ago to the present, observing the disagreement and confusion occurring throughout all the churches in cities and villages, took thought especially concerning the great solemnity of the Annunciation. And indeed, for the cessation of the apparent anomaly, especially in the ears of the simple folk who do not perceive deeply the things of the Spirit, the Church ordained that, if the Feast falls on these two sorrowful days [Holy Friday or Holy Saturday], it should be transferred to the supreme day of Pascha itself named after the Lord. In order that joyous things may be sung and melodized together with joyous things, the Church by economy prevented the mixing of the bright with the sorrowful, in order also that no disharmony might be shown between: 'Today He is hung upon the tree' (*Σήμερον κρεμᾶται ἐπὶ ξύλου*) and: 'Today are the glad tidings of joy' (*Σήμερον χαρᾶς εὐαγγέλια*), and between: 'Pouring out tears of lamentation over Thee, O Pure One' (*Δακρυρρόους θρήνους ἐπὶ σὲ Ἁγνὴ*) and: 'Gabriel to the Virgin the glad tidings' (*Ὁ Γαβριὴλ τῇ Παρθένῳ τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον*). But these provisions, as has been said, pertain only to the churches in cities and villages..."
[^315]: March 25: The Annunciation of the Most Holy Theotokos — Situation XXIII Conclusion (§§ 69–70) and Situation XXIV Opening (§ 71): Patriarchal Decree Justification Regarding Monasteries, the Order of Annunciation Concurring on Great Saturday / Pascha (Holy Saturday Divine Liturgy of Saint Basil the Great), and Opening of the Paschal Midnight Office. Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p511 (printed page 496) and facing English leaf p512 (printed page 497). Paragraph 69 concludes the canonical justification of the Ecumenical Patriarchate: while city and parish temples transfer the feast of the Annunciation to Easter Sunday when concurring on Great Friday or Great Saturday to prevent mixing sorrowful rites with joyful festal hymnody, the ancient Typika of the Holy Monasteries remain entirely unchanged, untouched, and unshakeable, out of reverence toward their venerable Founders and Fathers, and because of the distinct character and loftier spiritual asceticism of the monastic commonwealth. Paragraph 70 codifies the liturgical ordo when the Annunciation is transferred to Easter Sunday: on Holy and Great Saturday, after the Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX], at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 3 Resurrection Stichira of Tone 1 (*Τὰς ἑσπερινὰς ἡμῶν εὐχάς*), 3 Idiomela of the Triodion (*Σήμερον ὁ ᾅδης*), and 4 Prosomia of the Feast (*Βουλὴν προαιώνιον*); "Glory...": *Τὴν Σήμερον μυστικῶς*; "Both now and ever...": *Ἀπεστάλη ἐξ οὐρανοῦ*. Entrance with the Holy Gospel, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, and immediately without a Prokeimenon, four Old Testament Lessons: (1) Genesis 1:1–13; (2) Genesis 28:10–17 (of the Feast); (3) Jonah 1–4; and (4) Daniel 3:1–57 (the remaining 11 readings of the ancient vigil being omitted for brevity in parish usage). This critical editorial rubric confirms the hierarchy of feasts and concurs with Situation Seven of Saint John the Theologian (p. 556).

The rubrician specifies that if the feast of the Saint occurs on another day outside the period of the Pentecostarion, the service is chanted as prescribed in the Menaion: Katavasiai *Ἀνοίξω τὸ στόμα μου*, Kontakion *Προστασία τῶν Χριστιανῶν*, and Communion Hymn *Εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν* [Ps. 18:5 LXX]. Note on calendar limits: the commemoration of Saint Constantine can fall within the Pentecostarion from Saturday of the Week of the Paralytic until the Sunday of All Saints; outside of the Pentecostarion, until Thursday of the first week after the Sunday of All Saints (see the Calendar Table of Feasts). May 25 begins with the Third Finding of the Head of the Forerunner. Situation One details concurrence on the Apodosis of Mid-Pentecost: § 1 details Vespers: 3 Stichira of the Feast and 3 of the Forerunner; "Glory...": of the Forerunner; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast; Aposticha of the Feast; "Glory...": of the Forerunner; "Both now and ever...": of the Feast. Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, that of the Forerunner, again that of the Feast, and Dismissal. § 2 opening details Matins: Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; Psalter reading and 17th Kathisma [Amomos]; Sessional Hymns of the Forerunner and of the Feast; Matins Gospel of the Forerunner according to the order of the Menaion.

Commemoration of August 2: Translation of the Relics of Saint Stephen: Paragraph 1 concludes: Aposticha Verses: *Δίκαιος ὡς φοῖνιξ ἀνθήσει* [Ps. 91:13 LXX] and *Πεφυτευμένος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ Κυρίου* [Ps. 91:14 LXX]; "Glory...": *Χαίροις ἐν Κυρίῳ Στέφανε μακάριε*; "Both now and ever...": *Θεοτόκε σὺ εἶ ἡ ἄμπελος . . . μετὰ τοῦ Ἀθλοφόρου*; *Νῦν ἀπολύεις*, and immediately begins the Order of the Paraklesis. Section: The Order of the Paraklesis (Supplicatory Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos throughout the Dormition Fast, August 1–14): The Patriarch (or Superior) recites Psalm 142 [LXX] *Κύριε εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου* in a low voice [recto tono]; the Choirs chant "God is the Lord" four times in Tone 4, with *Τῇ Θεοτόκῳ ἐκτενῶς νῦν προσδράμωμεν*; "Glory...": Dismissal Troparion of the Patron Saint of the Church; "Both now and ever...": *Οὐ σιωπήσωμέν ποτε Θεοτόκε*; Psalm 50 [LXX] is read in a low voice. Then the Canon of the Small Paraklesis is chanted without Heirmoi, beginning immediately with *Ὑπεραγία Θεοτόκε σῶσον ἡμᾶς... Πολλοῖς συνεχόμενος πειρασμοῖς*, with 4 Troparia in each Ode. After Ode 3: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἐπίβλεψον ἐν εὐμενείᾳ*; the Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, with Choirs chanting *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times (4 sets of 3); Sessional Hymn: *Πρεσβεία θερμή*, and the Second Choir begins Ode 4. After Ode 6: *Διάσωσον ἀπὸ κινδύνων* and *Ἄχραντε ἡ διὰ λόγου*; the Priest intones the Insistent Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*; Kontakion: *Προστασία τῶν χριστιανῶν*; Prokeimenon: *Μνησθήσομαι τοῦ ὀνόματός σου* [Ps. 44:18 LXX]; *Πᾶσα πνοή*, and Gospel of the Mother of God: *Ἀναστᾶσα Μαριάμ* (Luke 1:39–49, 56); "Glory...": *Πάτερ, Λόγε, Πνεῦμα*; "Both now and ever...": *Ταῖς τῆς Θεοτόκου*; Psalm 50 verse: *Ἐλέησόν με ὁ Θεός*, and the Sticheron: *Μὴ καταπιστεύσῃς με ἀνθρωπίνῃ προστασίᾳ*, *Οὐδεὶς προστρέχων ἐπὶ σοί*, *Μεταβολὴ τῶν θλιβομένων*. Priest proclaims: *Σῶσον ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαόν σου*; Choirs sing *Κύριε ἐλέησον* 12 times; Prayer: *Ἐλέει καὶ οἰκτιρμοῖς*; Odes 7, 8, and 9 are chanted. After Ode 9: Megalynaria: *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν ὡς ἀληθῶς*, *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc. During *Ἄλαλα τὰ χείλη τῶν ἀσεβῶν*, the Patriarch venerates the icon of the Theotokos and, returning to the Throne, blesses the people while the Choirs chant *Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*; then the remaining Megalynaria: *Ψάλλομεν προθύμως σοι τὴν Ὠδήν*, of the Patron Saint of the Church, and *Πᾶσαι τῶν Ἀγγέλων αἱ στρατιαί*; Trisagion Prayers; Dismissal Troparion of the Saint: *Βασίλειον διάδημα*, and Theotokion: *Τὸ ἀπ᾿ αἰῶνος ἀπόκρυφον*. Priest intones the Litany: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς ὁ Θεός*, *Ἔτι δεόμεθα ὑπὲρ τοῦ διαφυλαχθῆναι...*; Choirs respond *Κύριε ἐλέησον*; Patriarch proclaims: *Ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ὁ Θεός*; Priest: *Σοφία*.

Both now and ever...": Theotokion; *Νῦν ἀπολύεις*; and immediately Psalm 142 [LXX] *Κύριε εἰσάκουσον τῆς προσευχῆς μου*, followed by the Canon of the Great Paraklesis. Gospel: *Τῷ καιρῷ ἐκείνῳ εἰσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς κώμην τινά* (Luke 10:38–42; 11:27–28). After Ode 9 of the Canon, the 4 Exaposteilaria *Ἀπόστολοι ἐκ περάτων*; at the third, the Patriarch venerates the icon of the Theotokos and, returning to the Throne, blesses the people (*Εἰς πολλὰ ἔτη*); then *Χρυσοπλοκώτατε πύργε*; the Trisagion Prayers, and instead of the Dismissal Troparion of the Saints (who have no Doxastikon), the three Penitential Troparia are chanted: *Ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς Κύριε*, *Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς*, and *Τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας τὴν πύλην*. If the Paraklesis is chanted on a Friday, the Penitential Troparia are replaced by: *Ἀπόστολοι, Μάρτυρες*, *Μνήσθητι Κύριε*, and *Μήτηρ Ἁγία*. After the Feast of the Transfiguration, the Dismissal Troparion of the Transfiguration is chanted instead. Original Printed Footnote 1: George Violakis documents that while the printed Horologion prescribes chanting the Megalynaria *Τὴν Ὑψηλοτέραν τῶν οὐρανῶν*, etc., after the Ninth Ode, and placing the Exaposteilaria *Ἀπόστολοι ἐκ περάτων* after the Trisagion in place of Dismissal Troparia, the Patriarchal practice of Constantinople strictly maintains the order noted above (Exaposteilaria immediately after Ode 9, and Penitential Troparia after the Trisagion).

Original Printed Footnote 4: George Violakis documents the patriarchal prohibition against the unauthorized chanting of Enkomia to the Theotokos: In certain parishes, where the Feast of the Dormition is celebrated with solemnity, an unauthorized practice arose—supposedly for the greater honor of the Theotokos—of chanting so-called Enkomia [Lamentations/Praises] after the Ninth Ode in imitation of the Matins of Great and Holy Saturday. The Great Church of Christ officially condemns and sternly forbids all such novelties and theatrical imitations.

Post-Apodosis note: Katavasiai: *Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς* are resumed, and Kontakion: *Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα*. Commemoration of August 29: The Beheading of the Honorable and Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John: Paragraph 1 details weekday occurrence: chanted as set forth in the Menaion. Paragraph 2 details Sunday occurrence: on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and Psalter reading, at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 4 Resurrection Stichira and 6 of the Forerunner; "Glory...": *Γενεθλίων τελουμένων*; "Both now and ever...": first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, Prokeimenon, and Old Testament Readings. At the Aposticha: Resurrection Stichira; "Glory...": *Πρόδρομε τοῦ Σωτῆρος*; "Both now and ever...": *᾿Ανύμφευτε Παρθένε*. Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, *Μνήμη δικαίου*, Theotokion: *Πάντα ὑπὲρ ἔννοιαν*, and Dismissal. Paragraph 3 begins Sunday Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], Trinity Canon, Litiya of...
[^393]: Month of August: The Beheading of the Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John (August 29, Concl. §§ 3–4, Fasting Rubric, § 5 Saturday Concurrence). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p667 (printed page 652) and facing English leaf p668 (printed page 653). Commemoration of August 29: The Beheading of the Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John: Paragraph 3 concludes Sunday Matins: Litiya of the Forerunner and *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; then Trisagion Prayers, Dismissal Troparion of the Forerunner, and Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": Dismissal Troparia as at Vespers; then Psalter reading and Polyeleos; Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, and one of the Forerunner with each of the Theotokia; in the Third Stichologia, Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner and Theotokion. Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, and Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection and of the Forerunner. After Third Ode, Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, then Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner: *Νῦν ἐπέφανεν ἡμῖν* and Theotokion; after Sixth Ode, Kontakion and Ikos of the Forerunner, and Menologion. Katavasiai: *Σταυρὸν χαράξας*, and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*. Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, that of the Forerunner, and Theotokion. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Forerunner; "Glory...": *Πάλιν Ἡρωδιὰς μαίνεται*; "Both now and ever...": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Paragraph 4 details Divine Liturgy: Typika and 4 Beatitudes of the Tone, and 4 hymns from Sixth Ode of Canon of the Forerunner. After Little Entrance, Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, of the Forerunner, and of the Patron Saint of the Church; Kontakion: *Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα*; Epistle and Gospel of the Forerunner. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Hymn: *Εἰς μνημόσυνον αἰώνιον ἔσται δίκαιος* [Ps. 111:6 LXX]; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal. *Note on Fasting:* Canonical tradition prescribes fasting on this day in memory of the martyred Forerunner, but allows wine and oil if falling on Saturday or Sunday, giving thanks to Christ our God. Paragraph 5 details Saturday Concurrence (when the Feast falls on a Saturday): on Saturday evening at Great Vespers: 4 Resurrection Stichira, 3 of the Forerunner in sequence, and 3 of Saint Alexander; "Glory...": *Γενεθλίων τελουμένων*; "Both now and ever...": Theotokion of the Tone. At the Aposticha: "Glory... Both now and ever...": of the Forerunner; Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection, that of the Forerunner, and Theotokion. At Sunday Matins, Canons of the Resurrection and of the Forerunner; at the Third Ode, Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner, as also the Exaposteilarion; remainder of the hymns are of the Sunday.
[^394]: Month of August: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of the Most Holy Theotokos (August 31, §§ 1–4). Detailed epigraphic synthesis of physical leaf p669 (printed page 654) and facing English leaf p670 (printed page 655). Commemoration of August 31: The Deposition of the Precious Cincture of our Most Holy Lady Theotokos: Paragraph 1 details weekday occurrence: order of service is as on July 2 (Deposition of the Precious Robe). In Matins, Katavasiai: *Σταυρὸν χαράξας Μωσῆς*; Kontakion from Third Ode: *Τὰ καταθέσια τῆς σῆς θείας Ζώνης* takes the place of the Sessional Hymn (referencing the original footnote on page 41 regarding the correct Kontakion). Paragraph 2 details Sunday occurrence: on Saturday evening at Great Vespers, following Introductory Psalm [Ps. 103 LXX] and Psalter reading, at "Lord, I have cried" [Ps. 140 LXX], 6 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": *Ὡς στέφανον ὑπέρλαμπρον*; "Both now and ever...": first Theotokion of the Tone. Little Entrance, *Φῶς ἱλαρόν*, and Prokeimenon. At the Aposticha: Resurrection Stichira; "Glory... Both now and ever...": *Φρένα καθάραντες καὶ νοῦν*. Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, that of the Feast: *Θεοτόκε ἀειπάρθενε* once, and Dismissal. Paragraph 3 details Sunday Matins: after Psalm 50 [LXX], Trinity Canon and *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Trisagion Prayers, Dismissal Troparion of the Feast, and Six Psalms. At "God is the Lord": Dismissal Troparion of the Resurrection twice, and that of the Feast once; then Psalter reading and 17th Kathisma [Amomos, Ps. 118 LXX]. Resurrection Sessional Hymns in order, but in place of the Theotokia, those of the Feast; Evlogitaria, Hypakoe, Anavathmoi of the Tone, and Prokeimenon. Canons: of the Resurrection and of the Feast; after the Third Ode, Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, then Sessional Hymn: *Οἱ τῶν θαυμάτων ποταμοί*; after Sixth Ode, Resurrection Kontakion and Ikos, and Menologion. Katavasiai: *Σταυρὸν χαράξας*, and the entire order of the Sunday Matins Gospel; then *Τὴν τιμιωτέραν*. Exaposteilaria: of the Resurrection, and the two of the Feast. At the Praises: 4 Resurrection Stichira and 4 of the Feast; "Glory...": Eothinon Doxastikon; "Both now and ever...": *Ὑπερευλογημένη*; Great Doxology, and *Σήμερον σωτηρία*. Paragraph 4 details Divine Liturgy: Typika and Beatitudes of the Tone to 4, and 4 hymns from Sixth Ode of Canon of the Feast. After Little Entrance, Dismissal Troparia: of the Resurrection, that of the Feast, and of the Patron Saint of the Church; Kontakion: *Τὴν θεοδόχον γαστέρα σου Θεοτόκε* (from Third Ode); Epistle: *Εἶχεν ἡ πρώτη σκηνή* [Heb. 9:1–7, see November 21], and Sunday Gospel. At "Especially" [Megalynarion], *Ἄξιόν ἐστιν*; Communion Hymn: *Αἰνεῖτε τὸν Κύριον* [Ps. 148:1 LXX]; *Εἴδομεν τὸ φῶς*, and Dismissal.
